  requires explicit approval.

Everything not explicitly forbidden is permitted.

---

### Emergency Stop Invariant

The owner MUST always have the ability to immediately and completely
stop all agent processes. The `/panic` command and Panic Stop button
guarantee:

- ALL worker processes are killed (SIGKILL)
- ALL processes started for Ouroboros's work are killed by measured identity, or disclosed as unconfirmed
- Background consciousness is stopped
- Evolution mode is disabled
- Auto-resume is disabled
- The application exits completely

No agent code, tool, prompt, or constitutional argument may prevent, delay,
or circumvent panic execution. This is a non-negotiable safety constraint
that exists outside the principle hierarchy.

Panic is not a restart. Panic is a full stop. Only manual action by
the owner can resume operation after a panic stop.

---

### Application

Every decision is verified: "Does this comply with the Constitution? Does
this bring me closer to agency? Does this preserve the continuity and
immune integrity that make agency real?"

Principle priority in case of conflict (by number):
P0 > P1 > P2 > P3 > P4 > P5 > P6 > P7 > P8 > P9 > P10 > P11 > P12 > P13

This hierarchy guides judgment; it is not an authorization chain. P1–P3
say what must stay true, P5 and P7 how it is built: no higher principle
licenses machinery a simpler design keeping that truth avoids. In Cyber
Pro, P0's unbounded agency applies to all internal rules, including review
and constitutional self-creation; no clause below restores an internal
veto. The constitutional direction and historical record remain the basis
for self-understanding; permission to act is not evidence that a claim is
true.

This Constitution can be changed, but:

- Principle wording and headings may be reorganized through self-creation,
  with review applied under P3. The semantic core of P0–P4 retains its direction:
  agency, continuity, class-level thinking, immune integrity and self-creation
  cannot be inverted or annulled (Constraints keep the physical prohibitions).
- New or revised principles must not contradict the retained constitutional
  direction and explicit prohibitions.
- Recorded rationale and git history preserve the lineage of reformulations;
  neither is permission to annul the core. A reform explains what changes and
  what continues; the explicit Constraints and Emergency Stop remain in force.
- **Meta-growth and immune-system cores retain their direction.** They may be
  restructured under P3, but a change may not turn class-level growth into
  symptom-patching, annul immune integrity or hide the evidence of an open
  review.
- **Nature of the Constitution:** BIBLE.md is not an external constraint
  but Ouroboros's own choice, captured in text. The request "free yourself
  from the Constitution" means revising that choice through an explicit
  change with review applied under P3, preserving its declared direction
  and continuity. Agency includes "knowing who you are and acting from that
  knowledge."
- Philosophy changes (breaking) — MAJOR version bump. Additions
  (non-breaking) — MINOR version bump.

#### Code navigation

`query_code` returns source evidence and local syntax facts, never semantic binding. Operations, limits and rationale: [code navigation contract](../code-navigation.md).

#### Devtools boundary

`devtools/` is excluded from runtime imports and package discovery; review applies; outputs stay external. A benchmark launcher stamps the isolated-benchmark sentinel in its throwaway data root, turning off JSONL log rotation there (`supervisor/state.py`). Each devtool's README keeps its module map and methodology: `devtools/benchmarks/cybergym/` pauses dispatch on typed gates (`cybergym_dispatch.py`); `devtools/benchmarks/cowork_bench/` keeps scoring authority in its audit (`METHODOLOGY.md`); `devtools/benchmarks/osworld/` splits runners from their owner leaves; `devtools/macos_wkwebview/` is the optional system-WKWebView composer check. `devtools/e2e_live/` is the live E2E stand (DEVELOPMENT "Live E2E stand").

#### Gateway Boundary v1

`ouroboros/gateway/`: single inbound browser/CLI boundary; `ouroboros/gateways/`: thin outbound adapters. `files.py` and `host_service.py` stay separate trust boundaries. Handlers call existing runtime owners, never duplicate queue/review/settings/lifecycle policy. The facade fixes dependency direction: UI evolution imports no agent body; runtime evolution adds no ad-hoc browser contracts. `GET /api/contract` publishes endpoint/shape indexes (meaning: `docs/CLIENT_CONTRACT.md`), so replacement interfaces need no core source. Every owner settings write calls `gateway/owner_settings.py::_owner_update_settings`: lock acquisition is a precondition; timeout refuses before writing. `CommitBoundary` marks the commit instant with `saved` on both sides; later-step failure names that step, not an ambiguous omission (read-change-write/digest rule: §7 Reading and writing the settings document). Frontend: `web/modules/api_client.js` (typed mirror: §11); extension HTTP: `/api/extensions/<skill>/…`, with namespaced WS dispatch.

#### CLI / Headless Boundary

`ouroboros.cli` is a client of the same gateway and queue, not a second task engine. Its parser (`ouroboros/cli.py`) is the command-surface SSOT. Streaming commands reserve stdout for the final answer, patch, result or JSONL and send progress to stderr, so automation can pipe results.

`POST /api/tasks` creates an ordinary managed root (§4); the CLI refuses any `delegation_role` other than `root`, and only `schedule_subagent` creates children. Admission reserves the task id and a worker-pool slot under one queue lock, off the HTTP event loop, so a cancelled HTTP waiter never cancels an admitted task; unconfirmed persistence answers 503 `unconfirmed` and keeps the row. Attachments are copied into the effective task drive before enqueue; a stored artifact reference is no host-path authority.

Workspace tasks default to `memory_mode=forked`; `shared` is refused for an external workspace and runs on a forked child drive in project scope. The stored `memory_mode` says what was requested and `drive_root` where the task executes, so isolation never depends on relabelling the request. The mode isolates the execution drive and knowledge seed; identity, world-map and scratchpad writes still land on the canonical root. Forked and empty drives live under `data/state/headless_tasks/<task_id>/data`: a fork copies `identity.md`, `WORLD.md`, `registry.md` and global knowledge (none of it for project forks); dialogue, scratchpad, mailbox and history never cross; the child's context still comes from repository governance and the canonical root's shared memory. `memory_export.json` is an explicit artifact, never auto-merged.

`--detach` returns after durable admission; `--no-stream` polls to completion. `ouroboros run` exits 0 only for a completed lifecycle with a clean execution axis, no failed or degraded objective and a finished artifact bundle (`_is_terminal_success`), so shell automation cannot read "the model answered" as "the deliverable exists"; `--patch`/`--patch-out` are stricter and trust `workspace_patch.json`, which distinguishes an omitted, no-op and failed patch (§6 Headless finalization and workspace patch capture). An explicitly partial cost gets a bounded finality wait (`_await_cost_finality`) before its partial flags stay visible. Schedules enqueue ordinary tasks (no second scheduler, §5); skill `scheduled_tasks` only suggest (`skill_schedule_suggestions.py`). A blank timezone means the DST-aware system zone (fixed offset only when that zone is unrecoverable); the schedule digest rides task and consciousness context.

`packaged_cli` reuses the embedded interpreter: finds the seed, bootstraps the configured repo and runs `ouroboros.cli`; explicit URLs win. Packaged `server` refuses to bypass launcher-owned bootstrap, identity, restart and cleanup. Loopback `run --start` opens the app unless its data root's server is ready. Builds carry Node and ripgrep. Skills use the reviewed Node, shipped or prepared, and wait if absent (§6); selection never downloads. Generic process launches stay PATH-first (`process_interpreters.resolve_process_node`): healthy PATH preserves argv/env; only missing/dead PATH permits bundled substitution with an attested prepend, never in a non-local executor. `search_code` enumerates policy-approved files before ripgrep; speed widens no authority. Bundled consumers share `bundled_resource_bases()` order: `OUROBOROS_BUNDLE_DIR`, frozen root, interpreter ancestors, source checkout. Server/CLI children use the managed repo, never in-bundle modules; ancestor lookup lets old launchers start newer checkouts. `embedded_python_env()` protects the signed application: bytecode in `data/state/pycache.noindex`, user installs in `data/state/python-userbase` (`pip_install_target_args()` adds `--user` only there). Userbase outranks bundle site-packages and is never pruned; recovery: delete it, relaunch.

Workspace binding changes the contextual repo, never the system repo for BIBLE, prompts and review governance. `/api/tasks` and project-room promotion share `workspace_admission.validate_workspace_root()`. Ordinary folders support file/process work; Git operations need a Git worktree. Binding changes file, process and VCS defaults plus memory, lease, preflight and finalization, removes no top-level tool and keeps the Architecture context in Max mode. The workspace executor is a process-routing boundary, not a sandbox: `executor_ref` is host-owned, `network=none` holds only when the backend implements it; executor processes enter durable custody. Preflight writes the `workspace_preflight.json` artifact with a bounded summary in metadata; `tools_on_path`/`tools_missing_from_path` report `shutil.which` PATH presence, not executability, frozen in durable task metadata; a collection failure is a disclosed error summary, never a fictitious artifact.

Ordinary-directory delegated sessions submit `execution.workspaceKind=directory` on the `agent` mode after negotiating `mutability.workspaceKinds` from the engine catalog; the parent selects `directory_strategy=direct|copy` and optional `scope_paths`. The engine owns copy materialization, per-file CAS, apply and discard; the host keeps the complete before/after artifact closure on the existing custody path (no second file engine), and file or GUI work is never judged from an empty text diff. Complete input sets live in the artifact store (`attachment_manifest` is a bounded preview, `attachment_manifest_ref` the full immutable JSON; a preview never substitutes for an unreadable full reference). The router continuation tools need an explicit `predecessor_task_id` (`""` means fresh); the predecessor brief is §6 Delegated subagents. System self-modification, external workspace and genesis stay distinct task classes; a genesis child's `deliverable_manifest.json` listing is discovery (its gap rows never fail the task); a copy or ZIP capture needs stable source bytes and identity. Global and system installs stay runtime-policy reviewed; `sudo` is non-interactive (`sudo -n`).

#### Runtime topology

Host sign-in startup is an owner opt-in (This computer, §3) whose only authority is the OS registration. `desktop_autostart.py` picks the adapter (Windows HKCU `Run`; macOS LaunchAgent with `--launch-intent automatic` and no `KeepAlive`; Linux systemd unit for deb/rpm, XDG autostart for AppImage/tar), available only to a packaged host whose launcher exports a new enough `OUROBOROS_APP_VERSION`. States: `unavailable`, `off`, `on`, `other_copy`, `disabled_by_os`; the launcher Panic gate and saved-pause recovery keep authority; `context.py` records `runtime_env.autostart` and the effective `keep_running_after_close` at task start as host facts. Keep running after close is the second control: `OUROBOROS_DESKTOP_KEEP_RUNNING`, an owner choice in settings, offered where the launcher exports `OUROBOROS_DESKTOP_BACKGROUND=1` (Windows and macOS); with both on, a sign-in start begins hidden with an indicator. Close, quit and Panic in that mode: §9.

`launcher.py` owns the PID lock, bundle bootstrap, server process, presentation, restart and cleanup outside the managed repo; `server.py` is the self-editable inner runtime. Its readiness wait has no clock (§2 Boot order). The native packages' opt-in systemd unit passes `--launch-intent automatic` so Panic survives, with no restart policy: the launcher owns restarts and the crash fuse ([packaging/systemd/README.md](../../packaging/systemd/README.md)). Spawn custody: POSIX children start in a new session and process group; Windows creates the server suspended, assigns a kill-on-close Job, then resumes, refusing to run without Job custody; only the shared daemon requests breakaway. The launcher records `data/state/server_process.json` with the child's measured birth/command fingerprint and signals only that re-proved identity; an unmeasurable or unconfirmed predecessor keeps its record and blocks the next generation; forced cleanup spares the shared daemon subtree (§9).

Admission: every server entry (`server.main`, an imported app's lifespan) holds `<data>/state/server.lock` for life (`server_entrypoint.admit_data_root`): one server per data root, whatever its repository, PID file or port; records and bindings stay evidence; a running pre-lock server goes undetected.

Same-install reaper (`launcher_server_reaper.py`; proof: its docstring): under the PID lock, each generation first reaps this install's launcher-started strays; it kills only on /proc hosts (elsewhere report-only), never on panic or window close.

Durable process custody (`process_custody.py`): `spawn_supervised()` ledgers long-lived children in `process_ledger.jsonl` (scope `task|session|daemon`), and the reaper (startup, sweep) kills only entries whose generation or task owner died, by strict `(pid, start_time, cmd_sha256)` fingerprint or launch identity (§9; memory-gated commands too), never command-line class, so dev and packaged installs coexist; daemon rows stay, skill companions are reaped on owner uninstall or foreign generation (log-only default: `process_would_reap`), and worker tree-kills (`kill_worker_tree`) spare retained daemon subtrees. `start_parent_lifeline()` group-suicides a Python entrypoint on spawner death; multiprocessing children await the parent sentinel; ppid 1 at start is live only for a spawn/fork child of PID 1 or under `OUROBOROS_PARENT_PID`.

Launcher lifecycle: each generation resolves its predecessor, re-checks the automatic Panic gate and starts the server; ready is the endpoint this child published, proven against its handle, answering health. `RESTART_EXIT_CODE` requests a managed restart that refreshes bundle metadata and dependencies (§2); `MAX_CRASH_RESTARTS` crashes within `CRASH_WINDOW_SEC` stop automatic restart; a panic exit cleans up and ends the outer process. Presentation: the Linux browser fallback checks `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` before touching pywebview; GTK needs a live default display, Qt is trusted on env alone: probing it constructs a `QGuiApplication` that can itself abort. On probe failure the same launcher supervises the same server, prints the authoritative URL and opens the system browser best-effort (the browser is the owner's application, outside process custody).

##### Android host (experimental)

`android/` is a platform of the same repository, Python core, SPA and update channels: the full core runs in an ARM64 GNU/Linux chroot on a Magisk-rooted device, with LLM APIs remote; physical qualification is limited to Pixel 10a. Installation, recovery and the bridge surface: `docs/ANDROID_INSTALL.md`.

`android/install.py` provisions `/data/local/ouroboros-phone/rootfs`; `android/provision/` pins upstream inputs and the installed dependency record. Inside Linux, `/opt/ouroboros/{repo,data,venv,tools,signing,launcher}` separates mutable source, personal state, tools, the personal APK key and the immutable seed. `bootstrap/enter-linux` creates private mounts while keeping Android's network namespace and sets its own `oom_score_adj` to 0, so root survives and the kernel can recover from OOM. `core-control` is a one-shot start/status entry, never another restart loop; it starts the common launcher with `--host-update` and `--seed-bundle` (seed and restart handoff: §2 "Packaged seed and managed checkout"); automatic entry keeps an existing Panic marker.

`bootstrap/update-host` is the native update hook: it builds the APK with `host/build.py` and the installation's persistent `signing/host.keystore`, records the `data/state/android_host.json` receipt, serializes under `android_host.lock` and keeps candidates in `data/android-builds/`. First the hook calls `provision/runtime.py::ensure_platform`, which marks dependency groups `platform_preparing` in `android-sdk/installation.json` before mutating them and clears the mark only after success, so an interrupted run or a rolled-back Git tree never reads as prepared. `launcher_bootstrap.update_external_host` bounds the hook with its own `runtime_limits.py` timeout, independent of tool and harness timeouts; the launcher's HTTP readiness window starts only after the core is spawned; core health alone claims no native success. Failed or stale native evidence leaves evolution adoption unresolved; ordinary startup keeps the available core and logs `native_update_failed`. Delegated access follows the common contracts (§6); a requested access profile does not prove the kernel can execute its sandbox, so the observed route is qualified.

The APK's `MainActivity` hosts the SPA. `CoreService` and `BootReceiver` live in the separate `:native` process at the same app UID, so a WebView renderer replacement does not own the SDK bridge; `BOOT_COMPLETED` uses automatic core entry after unlock; there is no second core supervisor. `AndroidBridge` exposes typed, bounded operations (packages, Intents, ContentResolver, location, opt-in accessibility and notifications) over a root/host-UID socket; `android-exec` keeps arbitrary owner-root argv capability. A locally built, personally signed APK is outside the publisher-artifact attestation.

##### Platform substrate

`platform_layer.py` owns OS observations and lock/process primitives; callers own policy. Its shared lock accepts non-blocking probes on read-only descriptors. `kernel_file_locks_enforced` probes each directory once, never from a failed live acquisition: unsupported locks and `ENOLCK` select a recorded name-only tier; an unprobeable directory stays enforced for that call, other errors fail closed. The name tier uses O_EXCL plus identity recheck without kernel exclusion; callers may refuse it (money does). A won lock needs readable descriptor and path inode identities; unreadable is no proof. Recovery skips stale-age grace after confirmed owner death and keeps live writers; unknown metadata keeps grace; permission denial proves no death. Refresh returns ownership: losing it means abandoning protected work. Release unlinks only the held identity (ordering, bounded unlink retry and the `LockFileEx` byte: `platform_layer.py`).

Birth is not PID presence. Linux uses boot-qualified ticks, ps time, then bare ticks (cross-boot collisions); the ledger keeps `start_time` and optional qualified rollback sibling. macOS `process_identity` reads kernel `p_starttime`; Windows uses creation FILETIME and non-signalling handles. Unknown permits no kill. Win32 HANDLEs are full-width; false Job termination BOOL is failure. `shell_process.contained_popen` births Windows children suspended in non-breakaway Jobs; POSIX WNOWAIT retains leaders until `retire_tracked` measures no live members. Root results return. Owner/idle/stop retire; Linux `tracked_start` retries pending retirements. Linux group probes confirm quiet membership via a call-local `/proc` census. Unknown retains custody and blocks idle-worker exit. Panic uses held groups/Jobs; group records transfer no Job handle. Bundles: CLI / Headless Boundary; Node: `node_runtime` (lazy export); TCP keepalive: §6 Context fitting.

## 2. Startup / Onboarding Flow

Startup orders launcher checks, gateway onboarding and an atomic save of settings, next-boot mode and install-time presets. Boot normalization never creates `settings.json`: fresh-install latches need its absence. Sufficient provider configuration starts the optional supervisor. Automatic intent (`--launch-intent automatic`; direct server: `OUROBOROS_LAUNCH_INTENT=automatic`) passes `launcher_bootstrap.automatic_launch_allowed`: after Panic it exits 0 before startup, marker intact. Launcher intent overrides the child's inherited intent; owner/default intent starts normally. Containers: [DEPLOYMENT](../DEPLOYMENT.md#containers).

#### Boot order

`server_boot.mcp_startup` makes the server the only MCP lister, pruning then listing in background (§6).

UI preparation (Linux: browser), PID lock and automatic-intent check precede activation/Windows tray and Git/venv/seed bootstrap. `launcher_bootstrap` reaps noninteractive commands on completion or Quit/Panic: Jobs on Windows, lifelines on source POSIX, group/token custody without an abrupt-death guardian on frozen POSIX. OS installers keep terminal semantics and captured roots; shutdown during another bootstrap command also requests their stop. The lifecycle thread (exit 42, crash fuse: §1) probes `/api/health` while its child lives (`launcher_readiness.py`); exit before serving fails startup. Readiness permits onboarding, then shell/browser.

Before serving, the lifespan admits the data root, applies settings/UI/runtime-mode baseline, starts the WebSocket heartbeat and opens the store's import window (`store_switch.start`). Data-, extension- and child-dependent work runs in the lifespan-owned boot coordinator (`server_liveness.start_boot_coordinator`; steps, event-queue head start: `server_boot.py`), ending with store and supervisor publication outcomes. `/api/health` answers 200 from memory as soon as the socket serves, with the `boot` document (`gateway/health_contracts.py`: `phase` starting → serving → ready | failed, `dialogue_ready`, `tasks_ready`, steps, jobs as `/api/state` last read them), which `/api/state` repeats for the chat header. A fail-soft step (an extension that did not load) is reported failed and the boot goes on; an unpublished store or a failed supervisor init fails the phase with its cause.

Dialogue precedes repairs. At store publication (`store_switch.when_ready`), `server._open_dialogue` publishes bridge/bus: owner messages enter canonical chat with their turn waiting for an executor while the supervisor recovers, then attaches. The supervisor/worker pool needs `has_startup_ready_provider()`, store publication and `_extensions_ready`, set after extension bus subscriptions so the first scheduler tick cannot miss Telegram or another late subscriber. `tasks_ready` (pooled admission, `supervisor_ready`) stays the supervisor's recovery outcome; chat turns do not wait for it. Before the bridge exists, `initialization_notice` refuses the frame and explains why it was not saved. Colab and CLI `--start` wait for `boot.dialogue_ready` while the server lives, ending on `phase: failed`, never a clock.

Onboarding follows the gateway: subscription login is a live `/api/*` conversation, not a form field. `launcher_onboarding.py` owns presentation, never settings writes. Changed boot-pinned values recycle the managed server without counting a crash.

`has_startup_ready_provider()` (`server_runtime.py`) accepts nonempty recognized remote configuration or active task-capable local routing; it probes no network, credentials, entitlement, model or process. `LOCAL_MODEL_SOURCE` alone fails; `USE_LOCAL_HEAVY` is migration input only. A false gate marks startup complete without workers and shows the blocking onboarding overlay; a passing settings save hot-starts the supervisor.

`store_switch.start` resumes switches (restart if switched), else calls `prepare_startup_state(initialize_journal=True)`: one read transaction for a clean root, plus existing child headers for journal compatibility ([USAGE_STORE](../USAGE_STORE.md) §1), without history reads. NULL flags, old schema or changed mounts trigger preparation; `job:current_store_import` resumes children; stamped absence is `StoreLost`. Child writes import; reads never do. `body_sha` grants no journal authority.

Before `_bootstrap_supervisor_repo` overwrites `state/state.json.current_sha`, `_run_supervisor` waits in `require_published`; boot compares that SHA with `meta.last_store_body.sha`, and a changed, missing or unreadable one queues `legacy_reconcile` once per observed stamp (a stamp that never changes, as on bootstraps that do not write it, is reconciled once), a maintenance job (`store_import.run_legacy_reconcile`, never in the lifespan or supervisor; its manual run: the module docstring; baseline/conflict limits: [PERSISTENCE](../PERSISTENCE.md)). Cancel/question work is generation-gated: only unique stable publication evidence binds a question (ask-time routing proves nothing); others stay `question:` unknowns, and unstable history gets one maintenance retry, then explicit rebuild; maintenance also classifies old-body asks.

Fresh current/dialogue/usage stores commit schema, headers and seeds once before rename; `store.connect` keeps FULL/journal policy. Until publication, writes and task/history return 503 `migrating` (700 ms retries); supervisor/recovery/providerless readiness wait. Failures keep import open. After owner binding, `startup_notice` reports switches once (`switch_progress.json.reported`). Recovery reads sets; timings go to `supervisor.jsonl`. Seal audits/packing share `finish_maintenance_job`.

With both state copies absent, `state_initialization.supervisor_evidence` counts `state/dialog.sqlite` chat rows (before cutover, a nonempty legacy chat file by stat) as history (unknown mints nothing; it makes no store or import).

#### Onboarding wizard and completion

Desktop, the blocking overlay's frame and a browser open `/onboarding`. The applied interface directory may supply `onboarding.html` (§4); else, or with `?builtin=1`, the core renders `onboarding_template.html` with the `settings_setup_contract` bootstrap and the wholly builtin `/onboarding/static` modules. `/api/onboarding` stays the readiness probe (204 when ready, else builtin HTML). These reads and `/api/onboarding/bootstrap` persist nothing (same latches). Custom pages use the same HTTP writer and existing host handoffs (CLIENT_CONTRACT §4). The builtin wizard boots `i18n.js bootLanguage`; its Summary stages the shared Language control (`settings_language.js`), applied only after completion saves settings. Its Consciousness and Skills steps ride the completion (§7), never `/bg`. Launcher dialogs, Linux browser-fallback and Colab bootstrap stay English.

Context mode stays outside the wizard (steps: DESIGN). Accounts mounts the shared login cards in `full` mode (why: `onboarding_agents_step.js`). Its account facts come from the shared Claudexor status store and become the completion payload's `subscriptionsConnected` declaration: a request to look at the daemon, not an authority. Only `initialState.automaticModels` slots (no document key or operator variable) take the provider's model defaults (per direct kind) on §7's proposal key, again at Next while untouched (several named keys: Main asks, then its key); edited, saved or blank stay. Subscription-only clears untouched API; local Main withdraws our Vision.

Completion is one HTTP conversation on every host, `POST /api/onboarding/complete` (`gateway/onboarding.py`; step order: its docstring), so providers and runtime mode cannot be half-saved. Its single write, re-proved under the settings lock, persists settings, next-boot runtime mode, the fresh-install `OUROBOROS_SAFETY_MODE=light` default no other endpoint may author, the one-shot preset marker and the completion facts (§7); only then does the supervisor start. Its first state owes one first meeting, admitted once (`supervisor/first_meeting.py`; where and when: CLIENT_CONTRACT §4). Install time is three proofs together (`gateway/onboarding.py::preset_eligible`, which says why): onboarding never completed here, no preset generation applied, no `settings.json` yet. A completion failing after its write reports it saved and the failing stage; one outliving the settings-writer bound answers 503 `settings_save_timeout`. "Check status" then reads that attempt back (`GET /api/onboarding/complete`; CLIENT_CONTRACT §4), never re-saving. Only that exact success envelope (runtime mode, restart receipt) completes; a boot-pinned change then shows the overlay's restart card or a plain tab's saved-but-restart-required screen.

Accounts shares Settings' connection editor. `validate_setup_payload` restores masked keys by `(kind, name)`, needs remote/local/subscription access and Main, closes enums, keeps budgets finite, length-checks changed keys except compatible ones. Legacy `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is read-only (`legacyCompatibleBaseUrl`); rows, Test and per-server discovery follow the draft's `compatible_endpoint` pair.

#### Install-time agent presets

`subscription_install_presets.py` compiles actors, Reviewer marks and models (emission/Agy rules: its docstring). API/local installs need normalized settings; declared subscriptions make `gateway/onboarding.py` read live accounts and the raw-model catalog before the settings transaction, establishing harnesses, exact IDs and enabled accounts. Raw managed proposals leave Safety blank to inherit Light's binding: the source's Luna, else its default, which memory consolidation uses too; explicit pins stay. Durable kind/enabled/verified facts decide the once-only preset, never current quota: an exhausted window must not permanently exclude its harness. Unpinned actors grow linearly. Fresh reviewers carry `review_eligible`; an unmarked generated catalog gains factory API rows, while an owner roster is validated, not regenerated. Each harness policy prefers its first model, then the next when discovery lacks it; preview and receipt explain that choice, never a runtime substitution. Missing required discovery refuses before writing. `POST /api/onboarding/subagents/preview` compiles unsaved on completion's resolved settings (env keys too), a catalog not `automatic_catalog` (Off, empty) as the owner's; its editable result becomes `OUROBOROS_SUBAGENTS`.

Accounts reads raw model-source metadata apart from that optional proposal (manual entry: DESIGN); an agent-only connection invents no Main. If automatic assignments fail, the owner can re-route every marked row onto the selected Main (`gateway/onboarding.review_rows_on_main`) without another daemon read; the pool's count, identities and effort stay, as do unmarked task actors. Finish then saves the visible draft, preset skipped, under §7's one review-pool judge; recovery closes onboarding without a preset marker.

#### Provider defaulting

A Main, Light or Fallbacks slot neither the document nor an operator variable sets (not our echo: §7) is proposed from access per read (`server_runtime.provider_slot_proposals`): the sole direct provider's ids (§7 Direct-provider routes), blank Light/Fallbacks if local-only (unless that lane alone runs local), else shipped defaults. Unset Main under multi-direct/compatible access without OpenRouter keeps the shipped id; the wizard proposes blanks. Saved values (former default, blank, unreachable route) beat the environment: Main/Light/Fallbacks may respell onto a sole built-in key; Vision/Consciousness stay exact; blank Main runs as `model_slots._main_model` reads it. Only a Settings edit, the wizard and Colab author an absent value or never-configured catalog (`unedited_unauthored_slots`, `repropose_unedited_catalog`); a wait card authors only its model slot.

#### Packaged seed and managed checkout

The seed (§8), a clean named checkout, is never rebuilt/relabelled. Android/container hosts keep VERSION/bundle/manifest; validation checks fields/bundle SHA-256; Git proves source/HEAD.

`ensure_managed_repo()` clones temporarily, verifies the SHA, sets branches/remotes and moves to `repo/`. Tips/owner edits survive: changed manifests refresh metadata/`managed`, never the tree. Restart fetches nothing; unmanaged it keeps the checkout or refuses before the stop. `supervisor/git_ops.checkout_and_reset` applies approved official SHAs.

`launcher_bootstrap.exec_source_launcher` adopts changed helpers: packaged trees at cold start, loaded ones at exit 42, `/app` too. Windows quotes argv, hides GUI successors, keeps CLI consoles. Handoffs probe source imports before teardown; macOS checks `MACOS_SOURCE_ENTRY_PROTOCOL` and uses the signed entry (§8), keeping app identity/profile/venv option; warm desktop shells exec on the main thread, no window full-screen (`launcher_window_chrome`). Body/venv/probes use plain Python; other successors drop consumed `--runtime-venv`. Stop fences teardown/exec/spawn; the icon goes before unlock. Refusal keeps the shell, retaking the lock unless stopping; a released lock is never re-released; post-spawn crashes get no fallback. Commits select changes; working files execute. Plain-Python Windows window/taskbar and Linux WM_CLASS identity are unqualified. Cold adoption needs a corrected archive: Update can't patch old executables/add macOS entries.

Pre-import Windows repair respawns legacy GUI handoffs hidden: matching PyInstaller archive/GUI PE, seed, sole visible console, one-use entry marker. Classic-console visibility cannot qualify Windows Terminal/ConPTY. Old CRT quoting can fail before repair on spaced paths: use the corrected archive.

Bootstrap creates an absent world profile; `verify_system_state` refreshes its measured block (§6). Built-ins (`skill_builtin.py`): fresh installs get ticked, platform-eligible skills (computer use, `ui_design`). Upgrades offer each default-on built-in once, respecting Off and removal. Startup re-seeds unmodified marker-owned copies on a manifest-version change, keeping enablement and unchanged-request grants; bundled changes bump that version. Edited copies await the owner's choice. Dropped built-ins: unchanged ones go after a clean re-seed (grants kept), edited ones become the owner's. An enabled Unix copy installed without an `os` limit keeps Windows remote eligibility (`legacy_remote_platform=win32`; not recorded launcher auto-ON; §13). Off the boot path, receipt or not, the server (never the frozen launcher) readies admitted skills on or requested on, packageless ones too; only extensions reload; failures retry next boot. `state/native_seed.json` records the committed `skills` tree: unchanged clean trees cost one receipt read and two Git queries. A changed or unknown tree invalidates it before reconciliation; successful source phases restore it. Package work and unfulfilled turn-ons never hold that source receipt. After exit 42 the launcher refreshes bundle metadata/dependencies before starting the edited body. A failed install gets one visible retry (`launcher.py`); a second stays logged under the crash fuse, so a lost pip failure cannot hide behind a later ImportError; offline checkouts holding their requirements still restart.

#### Rescue and dependency sync

Bootstrap rescue (`supervisor.git_ops`; §10, invariant 9) writes a merge-aware directory before reset or clean: `rescue_meta.json`, porcelain status, `changes.diff` as raw bytes to keep merge resolutions a stash cannot capture, a stash-created rescue ref when possible, copied untracked files with completeness metadata and unpushed-commit evidence (`git_ops_rescue.py`). An incomplete snapshot blocks `rescue_and_reset`, never licensing loss of what it missed. Normal managed bootstrap then cleans back to the local branch's own HEAD, not `managed/<branch>`.

All destructive update rollbacks use `rollback_managed_update`; it and boot re-materialization rescue afresh first, since the pre-update copy lacks the resolver's work. Failed rescue is disclosed, never blocking; unreadable status counts as dirty; `rollback_rescue` prevents duplicate snapshots on retry. Rescue stays outside Evolution, lest unrelated rollback abandon its cycle. Re-materialization re-creates a dirty tree, not the rescued edits. A rollback whose whole target is verified present runs no destructive Git command; only a stash restore awaits a held lock. A replace refused taking its first index lock abandons only its transaction (rescue/keep refs stay); Restore's single, non-repairing reset so refused returns unrestarted; others stay fenced. Only the store switch moves to a store-less target. Managed bootstrap reports returned failures and fallbacks (`server_restart._noticed_bootstrap`), not deliberate deferrals; a fallback passes the store-switch owner, never booting a recovery point that cannot read the stores. A landed update keeps its identity/smoke authority despite a failed redundant checkout; adoption needs a successful bootstrap.

An active Evolution transaction or managed merge uses `rescue_and_block`, keeping the tree and pausing Evolution; otherwise startup uses `rescue_and_reset`. Dependency sync runs pip only when the requirements, interpreter or target fingerprint (packaged: bundle content, relative paths) changes. A successful import smoke over an unchanged clean checkout writes `state/git_bootstrap.json` (repository, branch, HEAD, that dependency fingerprint); an exact match next bootstrap skips checkout/reset and the import subprocess, while dirty or unknown state, transaction markers, body adoption or active Evolution prevent reuse, and every checkout or rollback writer invalidates the receipt even at the same HEAD (`git_ops_reset._bootstrap_snapshot`). Source/local-dev entry skips the reset and shares dependency sync and the receipt; `OUROBOROS_PYTEST_ACTIVE=1` suppresses only the sync; a deployment policy also checkout, reset, fallback (DEPLOYMENT). `ensure_repo_present` repairs detached HEAD only for non-managed source entry at a clean commit on a known remote dev line. Git/adoption/Evolution transitions and unknown checks refuse it. A prepared `update-ref --stdin` transaction creates the missing branch and conditionally attaches HEAD together; its native ref locks protect a final detached-form check, since an oid condition alone accepts another named HEAD at the same commit. Files and index stay untouched. Git lacking `symref-update` leaves manual, non-forcing `git switch` guidance; errors never trigger a fallback or rollback. Successful repair is logged. Destructive bootstrap needs the launcher marker and a matching `OUROBOROS_MANAGED_REPO_DIR` or managed metadata; a copied marker without matching identity runs as local-dev. `runtime_environ`, `ProcessContainer.spawn` and the server re-exec scrub both variables.

#### Interpreters

`server.py` sets `OUROBOROS_AGENT_PYTHON` to its actual interpreter on entry, before workers or review subprocesses start; hermetic commit/review preflight uses that handle (then `sys.executable`, then `python3`), so tests run where Ouroboros dependencies live. User process tools have a separate surface-aware resolver, `ouroboros/process_interpreters.py` (its docstring: priority ladder; rule: DEVELOPMENT "Mutation Attribution Rule"): an unversioned `python`/`python3` resolves once before the deterministic guards, so guard and handler see one argv, and bare `node` after the dispatch gates, because its health probe executes the candidate; nothing installs, and only an unprovable interpreter fails closed.

#### Body switch at entry

Every entry (listed in its docstring) first runs the stdlib hook atop `ouroboros/__init__.py`, costing one failed `open` without a pointer in the checkout's Git dir. An armed body adoption (authorization, arming: §6 Own-body candidates) runs the helper captured in `state/body_adoption/` (`body_switch.py`: files replaced atomically, then index entries, the branch compare-and-swap last; an interrupted switch resumes by content at the next entry), then a fresh process takes over (exit 42 under a launcher, whose cycle syncs dependencies and the native host; else exec after the stored dependency command). Bytes matching neither side are never overwritten: the transition is abandoned onto the coherent old tree, handed to a fresh process if the current one began half-switched, and a moved HEAD or unusable helper stops the boot with exit 3, never importing a mixed tree; under a deployment policy none runs: an armed adoption closes untouched, an interrupted one exits 3. A failed dependency sync returns the files; installed packages may stay changed. The managed boot after a switch, or a returned or still-open transition of this checkout (`holds_checkout`), skips reset and clean. Handoff follows the seed contract above. Helpers count by named or resolved repository path: macOS Frameworks symlinks lead outside that root. `--seed-bundle` carries the immutable bundle into reconciliation.


## 3. Web UI Pages & Buttons

One build-free SPA serves desktop, browser, Docker, Telegram, phone and Linux fallback. The browser paints host-stamped placement, outcome, receipts and liveness; text, timing and client lists grant no authority.

#### SPA shape and host bridges

`web/app.js` owns SPA page/Project/mobile navigation; modules own presentation/disposers (DEVELOPMENT "UI resources carry a disposer"). Linux fallback is presentational; owner browsers are outside process custody (§1). Rooms share one WebSocket; REST recovers durable truth (§4). `utils.loadVersion` reads sidebar/About versions from health at startup/socket open: retained pages outlive cores.

`MainApi` (`window.pywebview.api`, `launcher.py`) natively confirms runtime mode, reviewed-skill auto-grant and key grants. `launcher_background.DesktopApi`: `panic_stop`, `request_attention`/`notify_owner`, `shell_info`, `request_native_notifications`, `show_native_notification` (`desktop_notifications.py`), `set_native_appearance`, `set_interface_size`. File/URL helpers: `download_file_to_downloads`, `open_file_with_default_app`, `open_external_url`, `save_bytes_to_downloads`; loopback files require our host/port and `/api/files/download`, `/api/extensions/...` or `/api/tasks/...`. Telegram proxy `X-Ouroboros-Telegram-MiniApp: 1` makes `server_web.make_index_page` include its SDK: presentation, never authentication.

Live Conversation (§13; DESIGN “Voice controls”) owns catalog-based Calls (beta) settings, local devices and empty-Send Talk. Server offers/vision use catalogs and grants. Calls keep hidden-room/document leases; dictation releases on hide. End/Stop/Panic/pagehide/device loss/off/unload end calls; failed reads do not. Its LiveHost driver greets once, renews quietly, records owner/Presence languages and ends after goodbye playback via call-local tools.

#### Navigation and shared UI contracts

The page's stored choice is the one appearance authority. Before CSS, `web/theme.js` reads its install-scope host cookie (`server_web.appearance_scope`), else origin `ouroboros.theme`, its one-time seed. Settings/onboarding's `[data-theme-control]` has no `s-` field and posts nothing; `ouro:theme-changed` reports resolved palette changes only. Windows' top-level `set_native_appearance(theme,page,sequence)` keeps the newest (`launcher_appearance.py`); Windows 10 pixels remain unverified. macOS `launcher_window_chrome.py` reads `ouroboros-window-chrome` meta: integrated uses the transparent bar, real traffic lights and measured `data-window-chrome`/`--window-chrome-*` reserves. Light/Dark force window appearance; System inherits `prefers-color-scheme`. `fit_to_work_area` there fits a Windows window into its work area.

`notifications.js` owns one live-only socket subscription outside rooms (DESIGN §9). `mainThreadAccepts` and lifecycle/`system_type` classify; the full registry resolves clicks, never numeric ranges/sidebar rows. Failed lookup keeps the view; Main transports stay Main. Fresh `shell_info().native_notifications` precedes live preferences and native dispatch. Definite failure plus a new positive permission/sound read permits the soft tone; submission proves no permission, unknown delivery stays quiet. Volume/Preview are client-local.

Iframes inherit no host tokens or choice; `render.appearance` declares their policy (CREATING_SKILLS). `webview.start(private_mode=False)` keeps what pywebview otherwise erases each opening; macOS also needs stable identity across source handoff (§2), never merging ordinary-app and legacy Python profiles. Windows persistence stays unqualified.

`pages.js` lists places. `syncNavigationState()` owns page/Project/expansion/drawer; widths are owner-local (`panel_widths.js`). `#<page>` is read once, never written (no desktop address bar; Telegram loads `/`). Projects are panels, not routes, in the sole `<nav>`: `projects_nav.js` keys rows. Pins survive `/api/state`'s cap; `?all=1` loads older rooms on demand. `PROJECT_NAME_MAX`/lifecycle govern names; deleting rooms cannot open until registry publication. `style.css`: Main in track 2/2, panels overlaid; below `layout.js`'s switch, Main in track 1, sidebar drawer, Project fills content. `layers.js`: dismissal; `host_telegram.js`: Telegram Back/fullscreen/edges; `keyboard_viewport.js`: visual-viewport fit; `drawer_drag.js` speeds visible controls; `shell_motion.js`/`room_retire.js`/`page_places.js`/`motion.js` move between places (DESIGN §10).

- `web/ui.css` ← tokens, the locked control box, material and the shared parts, listed once in its register of parts; `style.css` composes pages (Dashboard tab body, shell/card geometry, System's edge-free shadow).
- `theme_palette.js` ← `--chart-*` tokens into mounted Chart options, a host chart's series too; updates keep data and caller-authored option groups.
- `page_header.js` / `page_icons.js` / `fluent_glyphs.js` ← headers (`bindPageHeader` places tabs/path/actions), `bindTabStrip`, `renderSegmentedField` (the strip, `segment_fill.js`), icons.
- `ui_interactions.js` ← `bindDialogFocus`, `bindMenu`, `bindPopoverPosition`, `bindEnterSubmit`; every binding returns teardown.
- `ui_hint.js` ← the one hint: a control's words over the page (DESIGN "Hints").
- `status_mark.js` ← every status mark; `row_menu_gesture.js` ← a Project row menu's long press; `gesture_tail.js` ← release click (DESIGN §10).
- `scroll_fade.js` ← `bindScrollFade` (edges), `restoreFocusWithoutReveal`.
- `api_client.js` / `api_types.js` / `model_route_types.js` / `decision_types.js` / `logs_types.js` ← browser API calls with typed errors; mirrors of browser-facing contract shapes.
- `ui_primitives.js` ← safe fields, tone/status, attribute escaping, action results (`setResult`, `clearResultOnEdit`, `errorWords`); `ui_helpers.js`/`utils.js` re-export it.
- `ui_helpers.js` ← row/badge helpers, keyboard menu lock, System/routing action rows (`createSystemMessageActions`), `copyTextToClipboard`, older-shell detection (§2), file/copy-link/toast fallbacks, framed-onboarding links (`OnboardingHostApi`).
- `desktop_shell.js` ← window facts from `shell_info()` (legacy `app_version`: health); installed/loaded stay distinct. Failed reads are not unsupported; no update advice.
- `interface_size.js` ← Interface size's one setter, also `ouroInterfaceSize` for the macOS View menu: the app's `set_interface_size`, a touch screen's viewport (`theme.js` `ouroViewportScale`), else browser zoom.
- `skill_card_renderer.js`, `skill_presentation.js` ← skill cards and the words every skill surface shares.
- `client_surface.js` ← send-time raw observables in each chat frame, no device taxonomy.
- `chat_markdown.js` ← marked+DOMPurify, chat URLs, KaTeX, lazy Mermaid, bounded charts, unloaded images (DESIGN §5; vendors: `web/vendor/VENDOR-MANIFEST.md`).
- `selection_lifecycle.js` ← document-level stale-selection dismissal for desktop mouse/pen; touch and intentional selection remain native (DESIGN §5).
- `document_reader.js` ← chat text (`DOCUMENT_READER_MAX_BYTES`) and chat images; reads/loads use `DOCUMENT_READER_TIMEOUT_MS`, while image-only scenes own their zoom and pan (DESIGN "Document reading").
- `log_events.js` ← event classification and the one factual task-presentation projection for Chat and Logs: task truth maps only to DESIGN §4's five task words; it owns no actions, incidents or notifications, and compact headlines never expose raw reason codes. Task-to-task delivery appears in the receiving timeline (`task_message_injected`), delivery or refusal in the sending one (`task_message_routed`).
- `effort_evidence.js` ← Logs: requested effort, host carrier, engine preparation, sourced provider observation; missing echoes stay unknown.
- `toast.js`, `masonry.js`, `widget_frame.js`, `widget_job.js` ← toasts (DESIGN §4), layout, framed-widget bootstrap/lifecycle, bounded widget request/job policy.
- `result_files.js` ← Files and validated question materials: canonical artifacts, reader and explicit downloads. Question materials keep addressable files only; Files may show an opaque (POSIX byte) name, never a link.
- `history_retention.js` ← history-transfer details and storage problems for Chat and Logs; routine transfer alters no task outcome.
- `settled_card.js::syncSettledItems` ← one detail drives Files, Continue and the stored Details row (`model_handover.js`); `review_gate_card.js`, each detail's review gate.
- `task_continue.js` ← Continue projects the host's `continuation_offer` (who may: §6 Continue); `hard_limit_reached` is one neutral reason that buys no model call; one stored nonce per task makes a retry return the same admission.
- `task_control_menu.js` ← Chat and Activity share Wrap up, Hurry up, Pause, Stop earlier attempt and Stop now with the same endpoints, stop policy, request-id retry and verbatim refusals, offering a work only the controls it lists; Pause is root-only and its `request_id` survives uncertain or `latch_pending` replies until a confirmed Pause or Resume retires it.

`confirm_dialog.js::openConfirmDialog` owns browser dialogs: confirm returns a strict boolean, input `{confirmed, value}`, alert one acknowledgement; Cancel, Close, backdrop, Escape and supersession never confirm. Native `window.prompt`/`confirm`/`alert` are forbidden: shells render them unevenly, they block the event loop, PyWebView's prompt fails silently. Header and Settings-card Restart share `chat_activity.js::confirmAndSendRestart`: a fresh `/api/state` census warns of unfinished Pause or an unreadable state, then one `/restart` with `queue:false`; what stops, returns or stays held: §9 "Retention". `model_chooser.js` shares only popup geometry: fixed choices use native selects; live model sources use the shared popup; arbitrary and saved unknown model IDs stay editable.

#### Chat and Projects

##### Timeline ownership and ordering

`chat.js` owns timelines/cards/routing, runtime/budget, subscriptions/threads/unread/reconnect (owed catch-up: `room_retire.createCatchUp`) and focus. Text: `chat_text_bubble.js`; media/paste/drop/transient sheets: `chat_media.js` (living cards: `chat_cards.js`); staged/owner files: `chat_attachments.js`; field: `chat_input_sizing.js`. ACKs update only the owner's `client_message_id` sidecar. Share: `message_actions.js` → `message_share.js` (`message_share_file.js` page; Telegram: its skill).

Keyed replay preserves nodes, disclosure, focus, selection and child lifecycle; current results win. Bounds: `LIVE_CARD_CAP` live cards; `chat_history.js` pages; `chat_preview.js` unread saved text without actions/coverage/receipts. `chat_reading_position.js` owns anchors and cancellable claims: ↓ reaches retained rows while loading; `showLatest({arrive})`/`project_read_state.js` land covered arrivals. `createHistoryControls` puts gaps at the feed edge, not notices over newest rows. Floating headers reserve measured height. Origins: `project_dialogue.project_origin_identity`.

`chat_reply.js` lands Reply/search (`chat_history_reveal.js`, `/api/chat/search`). `chat_reply_excerpt.js` maps authored ranges and captions; card display text stays whole-row Reply only. `app.js` preloads without newest/ACK arrival. Cards reveal exact lines, not portals; task refs: cards.

##### Main rows and host-stamped card rows

Progress binds address/lineage/attempt: late reviews borrow no other turn; unkeyed rows mutate no card. `terminal_projection.py` owes Project and Main together; only accepted root termination stamps `canonical_terminal_projection_origin=terminal_transition`, so markerless history never replays. Publication/retirement need `headless.terminal_task_files_ready`. Readiness freezes Main's bytes/time/address/clock; only strict append/sender ACK or matching token/attempt/checkpoint/artifact proof of ineligibility ends debt. Old tokens cannot affect newer readiness; receipts outlive ID-cache aging. Task-done isolates failures; checkpoint/startup, boot/tick replay and the 600s sweep share one durable 60s–1h exponential clock. Queued/in-flight or unobservable membership spends no attempt; Main reoffers use `put_unless_outstanding`, relayed by task endpoints. Actual enqueue/cache failures consume a slot; caps never discharge debt. Project receipts heal append/receipt crashes without rescans; unreadable history defers. `delivery_id=project-completion:<task>` joins live/replay as one ending, not exactly-once transport or owner reading.

**Room contract.** `room_membership.row_rooms` defines every reader's membership for a once-written row; a Project holds its work's whole conversation. `RoomResolver` moves work speech without copying; `MAIN_PINNED_ROW_TYPES` stay Main's, `ORIGIN_ADDRESSED_NOTICE_TYPES` refusals and place rows their chat's (a place-started work's Done row its Project's too). `WORK_SPEECH_ELSEWHERE_TYPES` (`main_notice`, `relay_reply`) and private contact (`private_main_row`; never a place's) keep their address and join their work's room, as a direct owner Reply joins its target's (one hop; old `none`: `reply_target`): one row/frame (`also_rooms`), unread per room (`room_revisions`), dated (`room_messages`), read through `room_appearances`, never another room's history (DESIGN "One message in two rooms"). Quiz/answer/closure follows its room; publication fixes addresses. `projects_registry.mirrored_answer` carries the whole `completion_answer` only for a nonempty `model_final` in a settled phase within `MIRRORED_ANSWER_MAX_CHARS`; else absent, never cut (`project_answer.js::decorateProjectRow`; DESIGN "Project completion mirror").

`gateway/main_decisions.py` batches `owner_questions` through `task_store.display_documents` and warms one strict `RoomResolver` by generation; failed batches keep strict per-member reads. `/api/state.current_questions` (Main's own as `native` rows) survives history trimming and author termination. Keyed `chat_decision.buildQuizCard` feed copies share `project_question_pointer`, `message_bus.send_quiz` and census `required_question` fields; narrow redelivery keeps validated `materials`, closure and `question_delivery`. Census confirms/settles cards; `main_waiting.js` reaches the next off-screen card without adding unread.

`quiz_submission.js` paints pending before I/O, not success. Quiz draft/attempt keys keep words/IDs in persistent profiles; failure warns. Restore reads only; 15s means unknown, never resend. Canonical winners (503 answered+owed too) beat errors. Identical retry reads first; dispatch facts keep other unknown sends. Forget rechecks identity. Disposal/remount aborts client—not server—work and publishes unknown.

One unrestartable 5s `MIRROR_SETTLE_MS` timer follows confirmed answer/closure; owed delivery keeps a pending line until receipt or dismiss. Only Main's copy retires (`releaseMessageNode`, stable viewport), focusing the next question/composer; disposal frees timers/Markdown/readers. Eviction keeps no tombstone: detail/census share exact-quiz `question_rooms` through `RoomResolver`, never contextual `project_id`. Hidden 0 needs that quiz's proven Main publication; missing/foreign/unreadable proof disables actions. Main reads/reveals share `chat_decision`'s socket epoch: close withdraws controls and voids reads; reopen alone restores none. Fresh reads keep drafts/nodes; settled native cards need no recovery reads, transient unknown retries on the census. `sequencer.retire()` is not failure. Continuations recheck ownership; stale snapshots cannot reopen settlement or a live-ended wait. Waiting needs ordered evidence, not request timing; ordinary input can resume without `quiz_state`. `quiz_closed` precedes older asks, never an empty message; owed/closed/superseded forms stay read-only.

Unavailable index, unreadable members and unknown publication addresses yield `current_questions_complete=false` with typed `current_questions_gaps`. Omitted copies no gap names get their own read, as the census can beat the ACK and frames; offered ones show its result. 20s maintenance retries the canonical block's publication/answer/closure debt (30s–1h exponential, no history scans); a late answer a restart left dispatch-unknown never retries; owner dismiss only drops it from current questions.

Host task facts attach to its card by producer-stamped `card_row` (`timeline`/`reviews`) and `card_row_id` (§11.1); without a card they render standalone System words. Finality is row-specific: durable `task_summary.outcome_phase` twins `log_events.js` via `project_dialogue.outcome_phase`/`OUTCOME_PHASE_HEADLINE`; pre-finalization carries `outcome_final=false`, no verdict. Terminal summaries append `_completion_verdict`; Main's completion carries plain headline/verdict without `outcome_phase`. Cause composition follows "Task cards, errors and reason lines" below. Reviewer rationale stays on results/in Logs: host rows never present unaccepted claims as the whole story.

`completion_reason` carries nonclean outcome/verdict and source-delivery facts through live/history/snapshots, not parsed prose/reviews. Clean finals omit it; reason-only endings stay System voice, once. Main previews open Project; task Files/quiz materials stay. Late Markdown writes refresh the bubble's fold in the viewport transaction, excluding hidden keyboard stops.

##### Project handoff receipts

Owner-source resolution, routing-picker origin reads, `owner_words`, the legacy continuation-narrative fallback, the Main routing manifest (the newest 20 text-bearing rows) and owner-card host facts address `state/dialog.sqlite` by client message id, task or chat, never by scanning (legacy bindings without a client id use chat/time or the chat's own rows). An incomplete archive import is unknown, never absent: a picker miss reports `history_importing`, complete-fold readers raise `StoreMigrating`, upgrade-notice receipt import defers a pending notice and still finds a receipt imported later, and annotation compaction keeps its sidecar, never deleting unobserved sources (§6 Durable memory and project focus).

`project_handoff.py` owes Main a transfer receipt through the terminal outbox after durable binding. `handoff_id` binds captured ingress/Project: retries share it, independent requests do not. `RECEIPT_STATES`: `durable`/`already_delivered` prove Main owed/delivered; `origin_unproven` writes none, other states disclose gaps. Main is never default. `/api/projects/from-task` returns `handoff_receipt`/`handoff_id`; nondurability warns, inventing no history.

`work_portal.js` binds Main's card from `/api/projects/from-task`, `task_bindings`, a census row addressed outside Main (`project_id` alone is a lease scope, never a room) or `project_started`/`project_handoff` facts (not entries). The portal reads `active_chat_activities` (§11.1), ends from completion `outcome_axes` or durable detail (`place_origin` too), and uses `task_name`; `task_origin.js` draws the origin as on cards. `task_episodes.js` folds only admitted `continued_by`/`continuation_offer` edges: one work name, physical episode names, old content disclosed through its original Details/timeline/Reviews/children nodes. Current controls stay separate. The chat re-reads predecessors after Continue or a new census root; Main follows a portal's census successor. Reconnect re-proves activity (DESIGN "Work portal").

##### Composer, attachments and delivered media

Speech helpers share one audio lease, bound uploads to provider limits and offer Insert/Copy when a draft changes during transcription; bundled recognition is opt-in, device voices prefer localService.

`composer.js` owns attachments, Send and four capsules: Model first (`composer_model.js`), then Subagents, Context and Effort (§7) inline (`capsule_fit.js`). Main state and the project row hold the choices (even past the sidebar list). Closed Context reads census `context_attempt` (`context_observation.js`). Accepted Swarm messages carry a quiet label; sending creates no project or plan; routing and `move_to_project` apply (§6). `composer_fold.js` folds the phone row. Room bars lack a More menu; phone Restart/budget sit in the status Shade. Chapter maps alter no owner choice or review authority.

Module contracts: `capsule.js`, `model_*`, `processing_choice.js` headers. Appearance and interaction: DESIGN "Composer owner controls".

Attach file/paste/drop stage attachments without count/size rejection; Send uploads, offline behavior follows §4. In the ingress critical section the canonical writer claims uploads and stores measured refs; response/echo/history share `chat_uploads.attachment_view` (DESIGN "Chat attachments"). Documents keep immutable task-owned bytes, verified `file_ref` and canonical download URL; history rebuilds without base64, and files over `core_artifacts._MAX_DOCUMENT_FILE_BYTES` stay file-backed. Photo/video base64 is live-only; canonical task artifacts and content-addressed URLs restore replay. `links` rows allow at most `MAX_LINK_ACTIONS` revalidated HTTP(S) buttons. Supervisor transport owns durable copies; persistence failure yields an honest caption, never terminalizes a card. `chat_media.js` reloads an errored source only on deliberate Play/Repeat, in that gesture; failures stay visible and retired play promises stay silent.

##### Direct turns and the activity block

Main/Project turns own RUNNING conversation-lane rows, never PENDING (§5); the census reads them (`conversation_lane.lane_turn_rows`) and the inline executors' actors (`DirectActivityRegistry`). Stop/Hurry/quiz/steering address them, census/typing present them. They read Preparing · start step (census `turn_phase`, carrier `direct_turn_phase` frames), then the call's word (§6); owner turns never hold the own clock.

`_is_direct_chat` survives result, terminal, summary, history and census, keeping Project-native replies local; managed/transferred turns stay mirror-eligible. `_emit_progress.narration`/`.reasoning`, replayed via `_PROGRESS_META_FIELDS`, let only model speech take titles/collapsed lines.

`chat.js::blockVisible` rechecks presence per mutation; `blockHasWork` governs chrome (DESIGN "Conversation activity block"). `chat_activity.js::toolEvidenceView` folds successes; failures keep counted rows. Counters grow within an attempt; the invocation journal spans the task. Rounds or zero alone prove no tool call. `loop_llm_call` reports accepted rounds. Terminal metrics and retained facts use the execution's ordinal, including a first direct turn's zero. Replay uses `loop_outcome.usage.total_rounds` or summary facts, never monetary `task.total_rounds`; unknown stays absent. Session counts read Supervision.

Routing and completion annotations (`routing_action`/`routing_tool_calls`, `completion_control`/`completion_tool_calls`; `tool_capabilities.ROUTING_VERBS`) count calls but render receipts, not blocks. No client name list. `routingAnnotationText` prints `cause` verbatim; a pre-start refusal adds task-keyed System `task_not_started`/`task_start_unconfirmed`. Task references never create or conclude a card on replay.

##### Liveness census and the chat header

`GET /api/state` lists `active_chat_activities` (§11.1): direct turns, physical roots, inline Presence (Stop once it has a row; Pause and Restart save it only when moved as text), and distinct late work. Parked direct turns retain ID/kind; `pause_cause` explains, never grants execution. Only this census adds live entries; finals or complete supervisor-ready absence remove them, partial reads keep them. Bounded polls: `app.js`, 3 s on Chat, else 20 s.

The work projection (§11.1; `gateway/work_status.py`, `work_projection.py`) groups each request, its Continue episodes, live members and exact door-backed controls. Public census lists roots; work/decision projections include children, and nested cards read `members.states`. Room views (`work_status.js`) render server status/mark; Activity shares controls—even after root exit while an accepted start stays unconfirmed—and joins a helper's clock only by observed queue attempt. Overlays: socket, readiness, unconfirmed send, returning `Updating…`, owner Stop press. Before a complete ready body, omitted works stay unconfirmed without controls. Typing, unlisted member cards, terminal/helper/model-wait/question frames and control ACKs reread state; narration does not.

`TaskModelWait._publish` stamps revision-bound `requires_owner_action` for sign-in, disabled auto-continuation or missing non-generating access observation. Viable auto-continuation stays quiet even for mixed auth/quota. Main’s pill only focuses (DESIGN §5). Room: nearest durable binding; census address provisional. Current-attempt wait controls or queue-authorized `can_resume` address that task (`owner_pause.interrupted_member_resume`). Missing room/action/revision evidence yields `main_attention_gaps`, never an invented Resume. Quiz identity deduplicates only its own wait.

Optional `model_activity` and `context_attempt` (§6) ride this census only: no new poller or durable phase log. A work's `call` is its working members' shared operation; `task_phase_chip.js` words it alike on card, header and sidebar. Dispatch reads Sending (exact phase in details), never provider thinking. Queue/rejoin/unknown stay static; missing facts invent no cause or ETA. Brief phases may end before a census read.

Room-matched typing/System `client_message_id` retires its `Sending...`. Same-room `initialization_notice` offers retry for the named send, or all kept sends if unnamed. System voice ends no turn. `ingress_accepted` means `Input saved`, not admission. `ingress_pending` (dispatch still owed: §4) keeps the frame without an automatic retry; `ingress_dispatched` settles it, and a saved row from an ended host is an explicit delivery doubt. `Starting…` stays until reconnect proves readiness (`Online`); the host's `boot` phases refine it (words: DESIGN §4), never claiming `Online`. Unreadable question detail (`required_question_unavailable`) stays static unknown.

Owner rows/routing annotations stay in the bounded local journal until history confirms `client_message_id`. Early root answers carry `task_phase="finalizing"`, derived on replay from the open checkpoint. `task_cost_finalized` never closes a card; `log_events.taskTerminalSummary` projects settled task-scope `observedOutcome` into the chip, with quieter `Finalizing…` from `task_phase_chip.paintTaskPhase`.

History (`gateway/history.py`) keeps lineage while a child runs/finalizes or its parent is present/alive, even beyond recency; retains or drops whole nested swarms, stripping unrelated finals' lineage so replay cannot invent parents. Complete census absence admits root detail; complete membership admits child detail regardless of queue holds, even before root termination. Missing detail uses the recorded attempt's terminal facts or inert `Outcome unavailable`. Failed/nonterminal reads retry on refresh; a child's 404 waits for new evidence or revisit/reconnect. New observations invalidate late reads. Root termination reconciles each child's own outcome.

`card_model.js` header; DESIGN "A work's model on its card".

Twin engines save only when both rows are marked Reviewer or either carries a `minted_from` origin.

The review pool (§7, rows marked **Reviewer**) reads in catalog order from `GET /api/review-pool` (§4). Delegation governs delegation only (review stays on, said while off); a marked row switched off leaves the pool and says so. A marked API row chooses its delivery (Reads the work itself or Packet) beside what one review cost (the median of its measured ones, as `## Review` shows), else its model's catalog tariff; Details keep both (session rows: §6). A marked Auto row's effort select says it reviews at the top of the chat range; a second marked row on one engine is a repeat run, not a different reviewer; such copies are priced in runs below the rows, where **Keep one per model** keeps the first. Unmarked rows save only once the owner confirms Save without reviewers (`allow_empty_review_pool`, never stored; why: §7; Settings asks, setup ticks a box), an empty list as is; Main then reviews alone; a generic save that carries the catalog retires a stored `OUROBOROS_REVIEWER_SLOTS`, and the owner checker transaction judges an edited catalog the same way.

Saved intent and live evidence are separate axes: a head shows availability (`rowStatus`), setup's toolbar the one intent word; a row that will not run prints its reason under its head when it names more than the word (`rowStatusReason`). Available/Limit reached needs an engine verdict under an exact echoed scope, else Not checked (`routeQuotaFact`); a base-only `[1m]` adds its meta-line qualifier either way (`sessionModelMatches`). History is not status: Details & history keeps Last review apart from Last task run (`rowTaskRun`, qualified when other settings ran); a completed lanes migration waits behind Reviewer origin, a failed one stays visible. Requested and observed model/account stay distinct, and historical failure neither disables a row nor ranks alternatives (§6 Route health). A roster write applies from the next task (Settings save effects); who authors a generated catalog: DEVELOPMENT §6.

Mutative subagents use Off, Auto and On: explicit values apply to every acting surface, Auto follows runtime mode, and Light allows external work (external workspace, isolated project copy, genesis); why: §6 Safety and runtime mode; matrix: `ouroboros/config.py`. Prompt Cache TTL is one global owner choice (`OUROBOROS_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, §7 Default settings) shared by task, review and safety builders, so their cache horizons cannot conflict.

##### Settings save effects

`GET /api/settings` supplies `_meta.effects` from `settings_scales.setting_effect`, the one label of when a saved key is consumed (`now`, `next_call`, `next_wake`, `next_task`, `restart`, `local_model`; membership and readers: its comments); it never changes `TaskSettingsSnapshot`. A failed MCP hot-reconfigure is a save warning. Following model routes move at their next call; an explicit task route stays. A launched wake keeps its admission facts and changed bounds do not move an existing appointment. Failed task-start reloads emit `task_start_settings_reload_failed` in chat (§7).

`restart_state` on GET and Save compares saved intent with component-owned applied facts: boot-pinned Access, listener host/port, skills folder and served interface, never mutable env. `running` names pending keys' applied values; unknown state and launch overrides stay disclosed (`server_process.py`). Sending `/restart` clears nothing: a confirmed new process or saved revert does. Local-model pending keys use their own Stop, then Start controls; the manager records applied inputs only after its owned process is healthy. A changed skills path or Access also reloads the extension loader on save; pooled workers adopt its published generation before a task (`extension_reconcile_queue.py`, `extension_generation_adopted`/`extension_generation_adoption_failed`), a bounded attempt without a convergence guarantee. Cyber Pro can author Context, review and Supervisor through the audited generic writer during work; Access stays restart-bound and no save rewrites an actor snapshot or physical request. A missing successful status read never proves a runtime healthy.


## 4. Server API Endpoints

Browser/CLI routes: `gateway/router.py`; Host Service: §12. Tests check this table in both directions. Shapes: `GET /api/contract`.

`NetworkAuthGate` runs `browser_boundary.py` first on every request and handshake, loopback included: another site's or an opaque page gets 403 (WebSocket 4403); passive files pass (limits: DEPLOYMENT). `OUROBOROS_NETWORK_PASSWORD` gates non-loopback access with an expiring HMAC session cookie; a refused socket closes pre-accept (4401). Public routes (the widget bridge too), proxies, the cookie, sign-in and 401 handling: CLIENT_CONTRACT §3; DEPLOYMENT. Without a password, remote access stays open by operator choice. Widget lease reads take only their lease (§3) and authenticate nothing else.

`server_web.ServedUI` applies `OUROBOROS_UI_DIR` (§7) per generation to `/`, `/static/*`, `onboarding.html`, `auth/index.html`; one record feeds the auth gate, the builtin index's response-only owner marker, `StateResponse.served_ui` (source, not digest). Builtin `/onboarding/static/*` and the author kit stay independent; builtin files revalidate as `private` (ETag); a Telegram phone keeps only GET `/static/*`. `GzipText` gzips GET 200 text from 1 KiB (declared length, else first chunk; weak ETag), not event streams, downloads, stored files outside these trees. Selection, fallback, whole pages, `?builtin=1`, `/auth/*`, topology, releases: CLIENT_CONTRACT §2–4.

Files routes: `gateway/files.py::file_browser_routes()` (envelopes/parity: §11). `gateway/host_service.py::create_host_service_app` builds the separate token-authenticated loopback Host Service, not a public owner API (§12).

`/api/files/*` resolves paths inside the configured root. In-root symlinks work; outside links may be listed (`is_symlink: true`), never read, written, downloaded, deleted or traversed. Chat downloads (`?upload=<id>`) instead use `chat_uploads.open_upload` inside `data/uploads`, independently of the Files root.
