## manage_schedules

Read and change existing supervisor schedules. list pages bounded previews with offset/limit and total/next_offset. get returns one full authored definition and current lifecycle/outcome facts; oversized results stay readable through the persisted result source. update changes supplied name, objective, context, run_at or cron, timezone, and starting reasoning_effort in place; blank strings mean unchanged. objective is the future task's text, naming the skill or knowledge with its living procedure, or a note's verbatim words shown without waking a model. Every change requires a reason and is audited. Update preserves policy holds and paused state; its receipt says if an unstarted claim was reconsidered. A consumed one-shot re-arms only with a new run_at or a cron. disable/delete stop future dispatch; admitted work keeps running. delete withdraws the record, restorable for a while and retained until its accepted work settles and retention expires. Generic restore cancels withdrawal (the row comes back enabled, even if paused before) or enables a paused row; a consumed one-shot stays consumed. Held restore needs the observed hold_id; an unknown relation must first be resolved. Exact hold release preserves enabled/deletion state, pending task identity, money/deadline and other holds. Changes belong to a root turn; delegated tasks may list/get only; Observe cannot update; a Presence conversation lists, gets and deletes only the follow-ups related to its place: its own and those of the owner's work begun by answering one of its questions. Schedules fire only while Ouroboros runs, with one late catch-up after downtime rather than replaying missed cron ticks.

      "minimum": 1,

      "description": "Update: your label for the schedule. Blank means unchanged.",
      "type": "string"
    },

A missing cite leaves work from a place turn or wake your own. In Main the work is already your human's.",

## memory_mark

Mark what matters in my own words on one target: a chronicle record (node_id), a chat row (address), a task (task_id) or a retained source (source_ref); an optional quote is verified as an exact substring of the target; an optional anchor ties the mark to an action, so its words also meet me in that action's result. A room mark (the default scope) is in view of every integrating focus and of that room's helpers and session starts, a global one of every focus, helper and session start: each view, mine included, shows the mark's own text, its quote while visibility is full and its target's address; a mark adds nothing to my human's chat. A mark on a chat row of my human's own words also carries that row, verbatim and dated, among my human's words for the work to every helper, session, plan council and reviewer (never to a Safety check) of each work in the mark's room (a Main mark: each work outside the Projects; a global mark: every work). A mark, a change of its visible detail and its release also reach the works already running in its room (a global one: in every room) at their next round of the loop: roots, Main turns, wakes, Presence turns, helpers and nannies; the work that made one has it in its own result. A work parked in a wait reads it when it resumes; a mark wakes nobody. An external session a nanny supervises and the realtime live conversation do not receive them. Change a mark's visible detail (mark_id, visibility full/meaning, reason) or release marks (release_ids, one reason) when they no longer hold.

## memory_read

Read memory by address, as text: a room's records and the marks placed in it (first line: room, head and how many global marks are in force — they are in my view, not repeated), one record: what identifies it, its text, then its corrections, quotes and stamp (node_id; an account also names each source's version, what changed in it since, and the accounts a record informs; revision= reads a record as of one revision), a room's chat rows verbatim (rows=true with from/to, task_id or period), a retained source (source_ref), my human's words section for this work which its reviewers and plan council render (owner_words=true; their packets append the run's schedule text), or a selection before I make it (proposed_selection). A memory text's versions (source=identity, world, workpad or workpad:<project id>; version=<revision> reads one exactly, the current one too; without it, the list newest first, each line naming the version its write replaced) need no chronicle. Every page fits one tool result and its second line names the continuation (next_after_seq, next: from=…, or next_start): records older to newer, chat rows in stored order, a source's versions newest first. Choose the depth yourself.

## pause_task

Request Pause of a listed work through the owner's tree-pause control. The owner reads your reason under the work's name: say plainly, in one short sentence without ids, why you paused it, whose decision it was and what returns it: a time, an event, or only the word of whoever decided it. Later foci that list live work, consciousness included, see that sentence beside it; a press on work already paused keeps its first sentence. Started reviews may finish while the task pauses. Self-pause is refused: sleep with await_messages or escalate. To pause several roots at once (a general word to pause everything, say), name them in task_ids: one sentence for all, one outcome per root. A root already paused keeps its earlier Pause, author and sentence. The outcome arrives in your task mailbox.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "reason": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_id": {
      "description": "Exact id of one host-listed work; omit when task_ids is given.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_ids": {
      "description": "Exact ids of several host-listed ROOT works, in one call: each becomes its own ordinary request, exactly as if named alone, and each mails its own outcome. A list is never all-or-nothing and nothing waits for the whole: count the outcomes as they arrive, each marked with this call's list_call, and treat a root whose outcome did not arrive as unknown. An element that is not a valid task id refuses the whole call before anything is sent (invalid_task_id names it; invalid_task_ids: both task_id and task_ids given, or an empty or non-list task_ids). Consciousness and places are not works and are not listed. Besides each door's own answers, a list row can refuse: sender_stopped (you, the sender, were stopped after the call: nothing was done for this root, do not retry it); sender_state_unreadable (whether you were stopped could not be read: nothing was done; retry later or name the root alone); root_unverified or task_result_unreadable (the root's own record could not be read or bound: nothing was done; retry later or look at it first); not_a_root_task (a child: its root chooses its children, or name it alone if the owner's word names it); owner_paused_by_name or pause_author_unknown (a Resume found a Pause Ouroboros did not place: it stays; name that root alone by task_id when the owner's word names it).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "reason"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

Use the exact key (and scope) search_ui_translations showed; if the owner's words fit several entries and nothing settles which they mean, ask, otherwise act without a further confirmation. ## plan_task

Your plan for this work and the council that weighs it — code, research, a deliverable, a computer-use flow or an action in the world. Three effects, one tool. WRITE (free): goal, done_when, affected_paths and/or plan record a new revision; omitted fields carry over; identical content records nothing; affected_paths is required on the first revision ([] = the work changes no files; a path under Ouroboros's own body makes it a body plan, whose participants receive the constitutional pack). ASK (the only paid act): ask='council' sends the current revision to the review pool (Main alone when no reviewer is marked), ask=[ids] to exactly those participants — pool seats or any enabled catalog row (unticked advisers are heard, not counted); a body plan's first ask outside Cyber Pro requires a ticked reviewer and a reason when narrowed; Cyber Pro is free. Later asks use the named rows. Asked before any revision, an ask is a reading: participants receive my human's words, the objective with its author, the room and my message — no plan — and say how they read the request; nothing they raise then holds, and the first reading of declared body work is seated like a body plan's first ask. Participants answer in parallel the first time and see each other's answers on later asks; each receives the plan or its delta, the council so far, its own open objections, your message and your attachments. Each answer that arrives while this task runs reaches you at your next step; a pending ask holds no ending, and a reply after the task ends is kept in its plan record and shows as late feedback in this room when the room is known; the mailbox gets one frame when every counted participant has settled, answered or not. READ (no arguments, free) shows the current revision, every open objection with who raised it, who saw which revision, the latest contributions and the pending asks. An objection stands until the participant who raised it withdraws it (ask that participant again after you revise or argue); nobody votes and there is no verdict. An open objection is disclosed in your final answer; nothing holds it. The old spec/review_disposition form is refused at $0.

URLs are listed, never fetched. Files attach as read_file may read them, your own task_drive/artifact_store included, other runtime data never. Reads the system worktree via review_change(subject=worktree, surface=preflight, reviewers=[reviewer]), also used by commit_reviewed(preflight_reviewer=...). Informational, never a gate or an answer for the commit panel; unchanged worktree reuses its settled record free. No tests here; commit_reviewed runs them. deterministic_only=True requires source=worktree|index and returns free release diagnostics plus a separately labelled worktree book balance instead. Idempotent. resume deliberately continues ONE exact retained candidate (its id, owner task or branch) whose previous owner has ended. ## propose_payload_release

Propose that the owner release exact heavy files ONE finished task you may read keeps (database snapshots, VM disks, run data), only after you read what they are. You never release anything: the owner sees the proposal unchecked in Storage -> Free and alone decides. Name each file by its exact path in that task's artifact store with its role and loss, and the retained refs that keep what matters: the report, the method (scripts, recipe) and the result ('task_result' names the task's own answer). The host refuses links, files with another name, missing retained refs, overlap, and the always-protected classes: history, model requests and answers, reviews, memory, manifests, summaries, patches, chat media, attachments and source handles but raw test streams and a result-material copy its digest proves. An evidence folder may hold copies of model sessions or journals (a nanny's copies of its executor's transcripts): those are model inputs and outputs, never propose them; the host cannot tell them by name. A snapshot still needed by unfinished work is not proposed. replace_offer replaces one open proposal with a fresh owner choice; withdraw_offer closes one without releasing files. Otherwise files, retained and consequence are required. Old records stay. Proposal hashing reads every selected file once outside admission locks; large files can take time.

## query_code

Read-only code navigation with source evidence and explicit scope/limits. symbols gives local outlines, including qualified declarators; definition also gives labelled syntax name-field candidates. references finds exact-token occurrences (including strings/comments); callers filters syntactic callee positions, callees finds calls in selected definition ranges. These are not resolved symbol bindings: aliases and dynamic names need separate queries. impact accepts a file or symbol and shows occurrence evidence and filesystem import candidates; every depth hop remains a candidate. digest pages scoped file outlines with directory rollups; relevant_files ranks scoped files by task words. structural queries grammar node types in a separate bounded filesystem walk (Python also supports AST class names). Missing grammar or partial coverage is disclosed. architecture reads pinned repository carriers with query='<fact> <argument>': owner_of, domain_dependencies, facade_consumers, persistence_entities_written_by, protected_contracts_affected. Pages rescan current files, not an immutable snapshot. Use search_code for arbitrary literal/regex search; inspect source anchors to assess meaning.

## query_data

Read runtime facts, money, pack indexes, typed JSON/JSONL and verified blobs. No paths accepted. db, query, max_rows, snapshot and timeout_sec are op=sql only: omit them otherwise (another op refuses any snapshot and other non-default values); op=jsonl bounds rows with tail. Current SQL exposes tasks facts; use json/task_result for bodies. SQL defaults to guarded direct reads. Money SQL: read known spend from summaries (scope='global', key='') and inspect unknown_unmetered separately; summing the attempts amount column can miss imported string amounts in extra. Current-store reads hold the lock task writes wait on: at most 5 s; longer: snapshot=true. One SQL operation budget spans acquisition, optional snapshot copy/check and query; deadlines name the phase. The supervised child bounds functions that outlast interrupt, with separate startup/cleanup allowance. save_as retains exact whole-record bytes in the calling task's artifact_store with path/sha256/size/source. Projections use sorted UTF-8 JSON; store documents and multi-ID bundles are flagged reconstructed. format=text saves one selected string exactly. Complete tool output is retained before any delivery cut. kind=knowledge_history lists global knowledge writes (when, topic, mode, writer, focus, task, summary, sizes, change delta) without the note bodies, about 1 KB a row (raise max_bytes or lower tail); knowledge_read gives the current text. Results name their data plane; the owner's default queue files, money ledger, blob fallback and plane=canonical logs need the caller's existing read of each file.

## read_file

Read a UTF-8 text file from a declared resource root. With root omitted, relative paths use active_workspace; absolute paths select their permitted physical root, including user_files for home paths. Use max_lines (default 2000) and start_line (default 1) to read large files in chunks. The result header shows root:path and 'lines X–Y of Z'; each displayed source line has a cat -n style number and tab. Line numbers are display guides, not file content: exclude them when copying edit context. Prefer this over cat/head/sed-as-reader in run_command; to locate code first use query_code (symbols/definitions/callers) or search_code (text/regex), then read_file the hit.

## record_update_description

Save your description of an official update for your human: Dashboard → Updates and the Apply confirmation show it, and it stays after the update lands. Read the range first: query_data(op='json', kind='update_material', select='text', max_bytes=<its text_bytes>), and vcs_read(root='system_repo', action='show'|'diff') where a message does not say what changed. text is Markdown in your human's language, as long and as structured as the change needs; text_file={path, root} saves instead a Markdown file you wrote, trimmed like text (addressed as in read_file). For a requested description, including retry or Continue, base_sha/target_sha must match the original request. An independent writer can use a range offered in query_data(op='json', kind='update_letter'): checked_key, material.key, key or request.key. expected_revision is that record's revision (0 when it has none); a newer save is refused, never overwritten, so read it and decide.

## recover_image

Recover a previous image attempt owned by this task by its request_id. Reads retained response bytes or observes its recorded engine operation and reconciles the original accounting attempt. Recreates ordinary image artifacts after a failed download/storage step. Never sends a generation, uploads inputs, changes billing source or reserves another attempt. A lost create reply with no recorded operation id remains unknown. After a bare TOOL_TIMEOUT or any image call that returned no request_id, call recover_image() without arguments BEFORE any new generation: it lists the current task's recorded image attempts, newest first (request_id, model, provider, ledger state, times), from the ledger only, one page at a time. Earlier tasks' attempts are not listed and another task's request_id grants nothing. Listing sends, settles and acknowledges nothing and chooses no attempt; an empty list means none was recorded when read.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "after_request_id": {
      "description": "Listing only: next_after_request_id of the previous page (older attempts).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "request_id": {
      "description": "The original attempt to recover; omit to list this task's attempts.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## remote_mcp_sign_in

Sign the owner in to a remote MCP server whose calls return MCP_AUTH_REQUIRED (an HTTP or SSE server without saved credentials), or sign them out. begin returns the provider's sign-in link to give the owner; usually their browser then comes back to this server and the sign-in finishes by itself. complete finishes it from the full address their browser stopped on, when the owner pastes it. sign_out forgets this installation's tokens and asks the provider to revoke them (revoked says what it confirmed). Starting a sign-in sends nothing to the owner; whether and when to ask is your call.

      "type": "string"

    "server": {
      "description": "For begin and sign_out: the server id from MCP_AUTH_REQUIRED.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## request_deep_self_review

Request a deep self-review of the entire Ouroboros project against the Constitution: review_change(subject=system, surface=system) with one seat — the enabled catalog row you name in `reviewer` (review pool member or not), else the Main model. An API row runs a bounded read-only inspection episode, an agent-session row uses its configured access (writable sessions run in a private checking copy and retain evidence without applying changes); both receive the core memory whitelist inline byte-exact (memory is never receipt-checked). The report goes to chat and memory/deep_review.md, with the surface=system review record linked.

## request_restart

Ask supervisor to restart runtime after this task finalizes; confirmed acceptance holds new independent background work for Restart, never the owner's conversation (saved only in the final drain). An unconfirmed reply proves no acceptance. evolution requires its exact active commit receipt. A restart alone adopts nothing: pass adopt_commit (the exact reviewed commit of your body candidate) to adopt it locally at this restart, after the running generation's readers have stopped.

{

Only full evidence permits this adoption's automatic branch/tag push.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reason": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "reason"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## resume_child_task

After the owner resumes your root from a pause or saved application-stop hold, select ONE held task: a root may select any of its descendants; an intermediate parent may select its own direct children. Continuation keeps the same task id. Nothing resumes automatically and no fan-out happens: you name each child you still need, with a reason. The supervisor validates money, Stop/cancel intent, deadline and finite lifetime through the same seam the owner's Resume uses; the typed outcome is recorded as a budget_resume_child_outcome event. A held child reads status scheduled with a current_stop whose door is this tool; a grant removes that current_stop, so the child waits for a worker, then runs. Cancelled, completed or otherwise-stopped children are never revived; a child under a root that is itself still paused is refused.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "accept_unknown": {
      "description": "Copy acceptable_unknown IDs from the refusal in your task mailbox. Give a reason. The start may still run and spend money. Its request becomes lookup-only.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "reason": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "Why this child is still needed (recorded).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_id": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "task_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## resume_task

Request Resume of listed paused work through the owner's existing grants. A technical pause waits for the named billing or control record to become readable. The host rechecks the saved task's controls then. Resume a deliberate Pause when its named return has come or its author asks. A sleep wakes on what it chose. Your human's general word to continue returns what their general request paused; work they paused by name waits for their word about it or the return they named. It preserves spent money, clocks and review history; capacity and holds still apply. Only the owner can release a Panic hold. A list Resume (task_ids) is a general return: it lifts the Pauses Ouroboros itself placed and every other saved stop you may release, and keeps every Pause Ouroboros did not itself place, whoever is shown as its author now: the owner's (owner_paused_by_name) and one whose press declared no author (pause_author_unknown, often the owner's own from an older window). To lift such a Pause, name it alone by task_id when the owner's word names it. A child is its root's to choose (not_a_root_task). The outcome arrives in your task mailbox.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "accept_unknown": {
      "description": "IDs from this Resume refusal's acceptable_unknown. Give your reason to resume the saved task. Named local calls are never replayed. A delegated start may still work or spend money. Its request becomes lookup-only. Live senders stay held.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "reason": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_id": {
      "description": "Exact id of one host-listed work; omit when task_ids is given.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_ids": {
      "description": "Exact ids of several host-listed ROOT works, in one call: each becomes its own ordinary request, exactly as if named alone, and each mails its own outcome. A list is never all-or-nothing and nothing waits for the whole: count the outcomes as they arrive, each marked with this call's list_call, and treat a root whose outcome did not arrive as unknown. An element that is not a valid task id refuses the whole call before anything is sent (invalid_task_id names it; invalid_task_ids: both task_id and task_ids given, or an empty or non-list task_ids). Consciousness and places are not works and are not listed. Besides each door's own answers, a list row can refuse: sender_stopped (you, the sender, were stopped after the call: nothing was done for this root, do not retry it); sender_state_unreadable (whether you were stopped could not be read: nothing was done; retry later or name the root alone); root_unverified or task_result_unreadable (the root's own record could not be read or bound: nothing was done; retry later or look at it first); not_a_root_task (a child: its root chooses its children, or name it alone if the owner's word names it); owner_paused_by_name or pause_author_unknown (a Resume found a Pause Ouroboros did not place: it stays; name that root alone by task_id when the owner's word names it).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "reason"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## review_change

Review a change WITHOUT committing it: one paid reviewer wave on a subject in any registered repository, written to the review ledger. commit_reviewed alone lands in the system repository; other roots use this by judgment (it never starts itself and runs no tests: tests.policy=NOT_RUN). Subjects: base..head (commits), index (staged) or worktree (live) against base (default HEAD), frozen in an isolated checkout (only a synchronous caller reads the body's own staged index live). Mail mid-wave returns a pending outcome; reviewers continue, a [Review settled] notice follows while this task runs, and review_reference collects the original subject at $0 even after edits. The body is read against the body layer, anything else against the universal core checklist. Panel: outside Cyber Pro an own-body review names ticked reviewers, with a reason when narrowed (else a typed $0 refusal); Cyber Pro and other repositories compose freely. Omitted means the whole pool; an enabled unticked row is an added critic (alone, Cyber Pro only: heard, no verdict, no Required review). surface=preflight seats only the ONE enabled row you name (pool member or not): an optional early look, never the commit panel. subject=system (surface=system) is /review: one row (Main by default) reads the whole system against BIBLE.md and reports. subject=result (surface=result) reviews THIS task's result instead of a change: the reply (answer, default your latest), the files and effects the task produced, and what was asked; every seat answers one question, whether the result does what was asked, judged on the result, and on the method only where the owner's words or explicit choice fixed it. On a Required root, name ticked reviewers, with a reason when narrowed (else a $0 refusal); delivering unreviewed, the host seats the whole pool. A result revised after a review reached you is reviewed again only if you ask, delivery being your own acceptance. Auto composes the named rows. Cyber Pro composes freely. A child's own result review composes freely. Under Auto ask when another mind's check could change what you deliver or your human asks for one. Task review Off refuses it; it counts its own paid cycles. The same subject, surface, panel and ask return the settled verdict free (reused=true), even after a guide changed; after a settled wave formed no verdict they buy a new wave, except a fully answered adviser-only wave is returned as NOT_PERFORMED with reused=true, while a running or unknown one is collected, never resent. A verdict never locks anything. Returns JSON {record_id, aggregate, per_question, panel, rows, subject, checklist, tests, cost, reused, findings} (+ report for subject=system).

## run_command

Run a bounded foreground command in an allowed cwd; returns stdout+stderr and resolved cwd. A builtin as cmd[0] (cd, export, ...) is refused: use cwd= or ["sh", "-c", "cd x && a | b"] (also pipes/chaining). A background child (&, nohup) is no service: holding stdout/stderr it stalls the call until timeout_sec; it ends with this task (local POSIX runs only; start_service keep_alive=true outlives the task). A stop by pid reaches exactly that process (your own $!, start_service's pid); a name or command-line pattern (pkill -f, killall) also reaches other tasks', the owner's and this installation's processes. Prefer read_file, search_code/query_code, write_file/edit_text to cat/head/sed, grep/find, redirects.

Only outputs accept a relative '../' spelling, judged by its resolved location like an absolute one; cwd and file-tool path rules are unchanged.",

## schedule_followup

Create a named future task or note in the supervisor schedule table. Supply run_at for a one-shot ISO 8601 instant (naive = UTC), or cron for a recurring 5-field expression with an optional IANA timezone. The receipt includes the next due instant and this task's pending count. Schedules fire only while Ouroboros runs; after downtime a missed occurrence catches up once, without replaying every missed cron tick. A task wakes as an ordinary root through normal admission; objective becomes its text and can name the skill or knowledge containing the living procedure. With notify=true nothing wakes: the host shows objective verbatim in the owner's chat as a System row with written/due times, without a model call or context. Choose related work to keep the original verified money/deadline and Stop controls, or independent work; notes are independent. Either task relation can read this task's task_drive/artifact_store read-only, one hop, at paths you name. Root tasks only; Presence cannot leave notes. Independent work from a Presence conversation or work acting for a place names destination: without one nothing is scheduled. Elsewhere omit it. manage_schedules gets full definitions, updates a promise in place, disables future dispatch, or withdraws it with delete; withdrawal remains restorable for a while.

## schedule_subagent

Start a child on one objective; it returns task_id and reports back. Children may write knowledge notes, memory marks and chronicle drafts in their own name (the integrating mind accepts or rejects drafts: chronicle_write kind=decision); no child commits, grants itself tools or writes identity/scratchpad. Default native READ-ONLY children inspect repo/data/history and web/browser; no other writes or shell/review/runtime/skills. workspace_root: start folder, else yours. Read-only input_files: file/git_range. write_surface makes a child ACTING: self_worktree isolates eligible Git files (uncommitted too) for integrate_subagent_patch; external_workspace writes the SHARED directory (write_root, else workspace_root, else one new Git tree); genesis gives EACH an empty durable Git repo that IS the deliverable; harness work uses a private snapshot and integrate_delegated_patch. Non-acting sessions keep configured access in an evidence-only private checking copy; access='readonly' selects read-only execution. Runtime data is never a write_surface. Cyber-effective children inherit review/skill/runtime tools within task restrictions; nesting is capped. Children scheduled in one round run concurrently; on cache-write-priced routes each sibling started before the first responds pays a full prefix write. Native children can address you, siblings or any task in their tree: state what is interim, whom to address and when to stop. Continue: delegate_start(subagent_id=id, continue_from=run_id, prompt=''); work may repeat. Read the handoff before relying on it.

## search_code

Search literal text (default) or regex under root/path. Returns root:file:line matches with context; long lines include a read_file range around the first match. Skips binaries, caches, vendor directories and files over 1MB. max_results bounds matches. Use query_code for definitions, callers, references or impact.

    "bucket": {

    },
    "include": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "Basename glob, including brace alternatives (e.g. '*.py', '*.{js,css}'); applies on every backend",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "max_results": {
      "default": 200,
      "description": "Maximum number of matches to return (max 200)",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "path": {
      "default": ".",
      "description": "Subdirectory to search, relative to the selected root",

      "description": "Search pattern (literal or regex)",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "regex": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Treat query as a regular expression",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "root": {
      "description": "When omitted, relative paths use active_workspace; absolute paths select the permitted physical root (including user_files for home paths). Explicit roots remain explicit.",
      "enum": [
        "active_workspace",
        "system_repo",

        "task_drive",
        "skill_payload",

        "user_files",

        "deliverables"
      ],

    "query"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## send_user_message

Reach the owner while work continues: an opening that says what I will check and why, a substantial interim result they need now, a non-blocking question or an invitation to collaborate. Do not pre-send a duplicate of the final answer: it already reaches this work's answer room. A needed owner decision uses escalate: its card shows options, stays listed as waiting and brings the answer here. This tool sends a normal reply in this work's room, calls the owner back and leaves work running; routine news goes on update_focus, later progress stays in the card. For Presence work that room is local, not the place conversation: a connector reaches that, and the final answer only where context names that route.

'main': also the owner's main chat while this work lives in an owner-visible Project room, for an expected result, a decision or a substantial change to what the owner relies on (such as lost promised verification or unique data, risk to shared work, a correction of a reported result), even when a workaround means they need not act. One message: the Project shows it too, and it is read once; it is not this task's answer. A Presence root reports privately, with host-bound source attribution, including from Silent places: Main keeps its address, the Project its work lives in (if any) shows the same row, and its place never sees it. Delegated and agent-to-agent work cannot use it.",

## set_next_wakeup

Choose the next consciousness wake-up: seconds, how long after a wake-up ends the next one starts, and/or at, a named time; the earlier wins, clamped into the owner's OUROBOROS_BG_WAKEUP_MIN/MAX. A wake-up calling this sets its own next one; one already pending keeps its time; with consciousness off it is stored for later. A failed wake-up doubles the interval (up to MAX), a skipped one retries after MIN (an exhausted allowance waits for its reset or a changed daily limit), and none starts sooner than MIN after the last wake-up, boot or skip. Events never bring a wake-up forward.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "at": {
      "description": "A named time: ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset or Z, e.g. 2026-11-21T09:00:00+03:00; a time without an offset, or not in the future, is refused, and so is one at or before a wake-up already appointed (that one keeps its time). It stands until a wake-up appointed after it was stored ends at or after it, so a time beyond MAX is reached through intermediate wake-ups and one a wake-up outlives adds none; seconds leaves it standing, a later at replaces it.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "seconds": {
      "description": "Seconds from the end of a wake-up to the next one (the interval)",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## set_task_retention

Keep, or stop keeping, the saved materials of exactly one task when the owner asks: its work folders, copies, environments, review copies, result pins, call journals and saved states for exact return stay until the owner releases them. It never stops running work or lossless compression, and never covers that task's children. It needs the owner's own words: by default the message this turn answers, or one of your held owner_quote_handles. The result lists retained material, retired material or closed future document-ID reuse (`retired`), unknowns, and recorded thread/import outcomes (`releases`). A managed import's future_reuse_released does not mean accepted work lost its bytes; binding_unavailable or release_refused stays unknown. With release_unconfirmed the keep is saved, but an already started release may still win.

```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "keep": {
      "description": "true keeps them; false releases an earlier keep.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "owner_source": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "A held owner_quote_handle; empty means the owner message this turn answers.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reason": {
      "description": "One sentence: why, as the owner said it.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_id": {
      "description": "The one task whose materials to keep or release.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "task_id",
    "keep",
    "reason"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## showSecretHitl

Ask the owner to enter an integration secret (a bot token, an API key a skill needs) in a protected in-chat form instead of the chat. pluginName is the installed skill; fields are ids its manifest declares in secret_fields (e.g. telegram: botToken). The value is saved to Settings and is not sent in this conversation; you then receive only secret_filled or secret_replaced {pluginName, fields}, or secret_cancelled. The owner sees whether a key is already set and may explicitly replace it. Root tasks only; the task waits after this tool batch. Saving grants and enables nothing; enabled skills may apply new values automatically: afterwards check the skill's grant and status. Never ask for a secret in chat instead.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "fields": {
      "description": "Secret field ids declared by that skill's secret_fields, e.g. [\"botToken\"].",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "maxItems": 8,
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "pluginName": {
      "description": "Installed skill name, e.g. telegram.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "pluginName",
    "fields"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## show_card

Put an interactive card into your own message in this work's room (Presence-bound: local, not the place conversation). Use it when a control saves the owner work a text answer would leave to them: a choice with details, a small form, a compact dashboard or checklist, a calculator or simulation. Keep ordinary answers as text.

Exactly one body. components: a declarative tree the host draws (markdown, metric, callout, kv, key_value, table, chart, progress, code, json, status, group, tabs, map, calendar, kanban, image, audio, video, gallery, action, form; no routes); each action and form binds submit: {id, once?} and data fills the path-reading components. An image takes file: the path of a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP you wrote (absolute, or relative to your workspace; a card's images at most 2 MiB together), which the host copies into the card, or src: an inline data: URI, as audio and video do. widget: {skill, tab_id, input?} shows an installed live skill's widget inline. app: {path} or {html} of a self-contained HTML page (at most 512 KiB) that runs sandboxed: it cannot fetch or load resources, and loading another page closes it. On most devices it shares the owner's page thread: keep heavy computation in a blob: Worker, never a long synchronous loop.

A press on an action or form comes back to you as a [Card input] message with its values (after your task ended, as the owner's message in this chat: the pressed label and values, as a reply to the card); once: true accepts only the first press. An app's submit only fills the owner's draft, which the owner sends. fallback_text is the plain version for Telegram, exports and any surface that cannot draw the card. replace=<card_id> updates an earlier card of this chat in place.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "app": {
      "properties": {
        "html": {
          "description": "The page itself, instead of path.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "path": {
          "description": "An HTML file you wrote (absolute, or relative to your workspace).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "components": {
      "description": "Declarative component tree; action/form use submit: {id: [a-z0-9_]{1,40}, once?: boolean}.",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "data": {
      "description": "Values the components' path fields read (components only).",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "fallback_text": {
      "description": "The card's content as plain text (at most 4000 characters), shown wherever the card cannot render.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "replace": {
      "description": "card_id of an earlier card of this chat to update in place.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "title": {
      "description": "Card heading (at most 120 characters).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "widget": {
      "properties": {
        "input": {
          "description": "Optional input the widget receives.",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "skill": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "tab_id": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "skill",
        "tab_id"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "title",
    "fallback_text"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## skill_exec

Run one manifest-declared script of a type=script skill. The skill must be enabled and its review_gate must permit the current bytes: outside Cyber Pro, a current executable reviewer verdict or a qualified author acceptance of these exact bytes (the reviewer status may then still be pending or stale); Cyber Pro leaves it to Ouroboros's judgment. Requested key/permission grants and isolated dependencies still apply. Only type=script skills execute via this substrate — type=instruction skills are catalogued + reviewable but have no executable payload by design; type=extension skills expose their own tools, routes and handlers instead (calling skill_exec on an extension returns SKILL_EXEC_EXTENSION pointing at that surface). The ``script`` argument must match a ``name`` entry in the manifest's ``scripts:`` array (SKILL.md body and assets/* are reviewed content but not executable). Runtime allowlist: python/python3/bash/node/deno/ruby/go. The subprocess runs with cwd=skill_dir, a scrubbed env (env_from_settings keys only), panic-kill tracking, and a timeout from the manifest (capped at 300s). OUROBOROS_RUNTIME_MODE does not gate execution — light, advanced, and pro all let reviewed + enabled skills run. Light still blocks repo self-modification and the runtime_mode elevation ratchet.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "args": {
      "description": "Optional argv for the script.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "script": {
      "description": "Relative path of the script inside the skill directory (e.g. 'scripts/fetch.py'). Absolute paths and '..' traversal are rejected.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "skill": {
      "description": "Skill name (directory name in OUROBOROS_SKILLS_REPO_PATH).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "skill",
    "script"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## skill_owner_action

Ordinary Repair does not imply these actions. Interpret the referenced owner's actual words; do not invent a source or treat an ID as approval. Host validates source membership, caller and revision. Attestation still runs deterministic preflight and is unavailable for ClawHub/native payloads. Use toggle_skill for ordinary enable/disable.

## skill_preflight

Read-only payload syntax/contract validator for one skill. Runs Python compile() (no __pycache__), bash -n, and node syntax checks (widget entries stay classic unless entry_type: module declares ESM) on every reviewable file, or just `paths`, plus a manifest parse, declared widget file existence, and render-schema validation. Cheap and offline (no LLM, no review.json mutation, no review status change). Skill-development tasks use this before calling skill_review so silly syntax errors are caught without spending the review panel's tokens. Argv-only subprocess invocation, cwd=skill_dir, scrubbed env, 30s per-file cap, panic-tracked process group.

```json

    "paths": {

      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "skill": {
      "description": "Skill name (directory basename in the skills tree).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "skill"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## skill_review

Run skill review by the review panel (paid; an unchanged snapshot's verdict replays free) on one external skill package using the review pool configuration and scored against the Skill Review Checklist section in docs/CHECKLISTS.md. Persists the verdict to data/state/skills/<name>/review.json with a content hash so a later edit invalidates the review automatically. Max Review Cycles semantics: an identical request never buys a new panel over a verdict — the settled verdict of the same subject REPLAYS free, keyed by the shared reuse identity (the subject's bytes and rules, the assigned seats, the answer contract and the round: rebuttal, goal, scope), so only changed content, a changed panel or contract, or a NEW rebuttal dispatches reviewers again. After a settled wave formed no verdict, the identical request is a new paid wave; a running or unknown one is collected, never sent again. The shared OUROBOROS_REVIEW_MAX_CYCLES ceiling bounds PAID panel dispatches per ceiling key (root task for task-driven reviews; the current content snapshot for the manual lane); on exhaustion the review is refused free with a typed review_cycles_exhausted event and stays honestly PENDING — no verdict is fabricated. Whether the payload may run is the skill's review_gate; Cyber Pro leaves it to Ouroboros's judgment, with the review as evidence, not a PASS.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "author_disposition": {
      "description": "Optional author finish for the current content hash. Keeps original critic evidence; changed or unavailable-review cases require current deterministic preflight. For terminal partial-feedback or unavailable outcomes, pass the returned review_reference.",
      "enum": [
        "accepted",
        "rejected",
        "partial",
        "deferred"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "author_rationale": {
      "description": "Required when author_disposition is supplied; explain why the author accepts, rejects, partially accepts, or defers the raw findings.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "continue_seats": {
      "description": "With review_reference naming its record_id and content_hash: Continue stopped session reviewers of the referenced review, each named exactly as its continuable_seats offer gives it. Each choice starts one successor run of the same seat in the same wave from the seat's original request (model, effort, account choice, access, output contract) within the original remaining time and current limits; repeating it rejoins that successor. Running, unknown or answered seats are refused at $0; a fresh review stays a separate act. The record's own bytes are collected; changed bytes gain nothing.",
      "items": {
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "operation_id": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "seat_id": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "seat_id",
          "operation_id"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "reason": {
      "description": "Why these reviewers; required for a narrowed panel outside Cyber Pro, including a re-review after blockers.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "review_rebuttal": {
      "description": "Optional rebuttal to prior review findings. Use only when you have code-grounded evidence that a previous finding was a false positive or already addressed. The rebuttal is identified by CONTENT: its sha256 buys exactly ONE paid panel wave when new to the current snapshot's streak; repeating an already-adjudicated rebuttal replays the recorded verdict free, and no rebuttal buys past the paid-cycle ceiling.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "review_reference": {
      "description": "For a review that formed no verdict (quorum failed, nothing dispatched): the exact reference returned by that skill review (its job_id or record_id with the content_hash). A review still running is not unavailable. With continue_seats (record_id and content_hash) it continues that review's stopped seats on its recorded bytes instead.",
      "properties": {
        "content_hash": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "job_id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "record_id": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "content_hash"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "reviewers": {
      "description": "Enabled row ids/handles; omitted means the whole pool. Outside Cyber Pro name at least one ticked reviewer, with a reason when you name fewer than all. Unticked advisers are heard, not counted. Cyber Pro composes freely.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "skill": {
      "description": "Skill name (directory name in OUROBOROS_SKILLS_REPO_PATH).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "skill"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## stage_pr_merge

Stage a no-fast-forward merge of an integration branch into the body's working branch WITHOUT committing (git merge --no-ff --no-commit). Sets MERGE_HEAD so commit_reviewed creates a proper merge commit with both parents. Target is branch_dev (the bound candidate branch during self-development), the branch commit_reviewed commits on: it keeps the staged merge there and refuses to switch branches while a merge is pending. The integration-branch history (with original author commits) is permanently linked. Finalize via commit_reviewed.

}
```

## start_task

Start a NEW, separate independent work with its own task id and card. The work reading the current request already exists and can do that request itself. move_to_project places THIS work in a room with the same id. For an EXISTING artifact, ground-truth its existence with one cheap probe (list_skills/list_files): memory of past work is not evidence it still exists. Give the separate work a short title and objective. project_name creates a named room; project_id selects an existing room. workspace_root selects its folder; workspace='none' opts out of the room's default folder. From a Presence conversation or work acting for a place, name where each new work belongs with destination; without one nothing starts. Elsewhere omit it. Set context_requires_development=true only when the task itself needs the whole development handbook in every mode, never for its subject; a route too small for it refuses the task. A durable pending intent is recorded but not yet confirmed; inspect its recorded outcome before explicitly retrying.

## tree_note

Post a coordination entry, a beacon to your parent, or a child-result decision to the SHARED task-tree ledger (the swarm blackboard, scoped to root_task_id — visible to the parent and all siblings/descendants of THIS task tree). Use it to publish the shared frame BEFORE fanning out interdependent children and to coordinate while they run. kind: contract|decision|fact|note (coordination) or milestone|partial_finding|blocker|question|interface_contract|review_requested|delegation_constraint (child->parent beacon). blocker/question/interface_contract/review_requested/delegation_constraint (or needs_parent_attention=true) surface an early return in the parent's wait. Domain-agnostic: 'contract' = code APIs OR presentation section-ownership OR a research claim schema — the seam for THIS task. Keep entries short; bulk detail belongs in artifacts.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "kind": {
      "enum": [
        "contract",
        "decision",
        "fact",
        "note",
        "milestone",
        "partial_finding",
        "blocker",
        "question",
        "interface_contract",
        "review_requested",
        "delegation_constraint"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "needs_parent_attention": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Force a parent early-wait return (implied by blocker/question/interface_contract/review_requested).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "payload": {
      "description": "Structured payload. For review_requested, provide exactly evidence_ref and evidence_sha256; this records a non-blocking exact-evidence request and never starts a reviewer. If the parent launches a check, it carries that hash into the existing accounting/dedup path. Required for delegation_constraint. For a parent decision about a direct child result, set type=child_result_disposition, child_task_id, disposition, and the exact SHA-256 shown by child evidence; tree_note text is the rationale. To disposition MANY children in one call, set type=child_result_disposition and a children array of {child_task_id, disposition, child_result_sha256} entries (one shared rationale; each entry is validated exactly like the single form).",
      "properties": {
        "child_result_sha256": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "child_task_id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "children": {
          "description": "Batch child dispositions: entries of {child_task_id, disposition, child_result_sha256}.",
          "items": {
            "properties": {
              "child_result_sha256": {
                "type": "string"
              },
              "child_task_id": {
                "type": "string"
              },
              "disposition": {
                "description": "integrated = consumed by this answer (item closes); irrelevant = not needed here (the child result stays as evidence; item closes); deferred = STILL OWED: your terminal answer reads degraded/best_effort until you re-disposition this exact child_result_sha256. Integrated/irrelevant also let the host release the child's disposable scratch; until then it waits for your end, Continues included: while a step or sibling reads it by a path you passed (the host cannot see such paths), stay deferred or save what must outlive it.",
                "enum": [
                  "deferred",
                  "integrated",
                  "irrelevant"
                ],
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "required": [
              "child_task_id",
              "disposition",
              "child_result_sha256"
            ],
            "type": "object"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "constraint_id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "created_by": {
          "description": "Display label. The host records the emitting task.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "directive": {
          "enum": [
            "halt_fanout",
            "cap_children",
            "require_lane",
            "block_surface"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        "disposition": {
          "description": "integrated = consumed by this answer (item closes); irrelevant = not needed here (the child result stays as evidence; item closes); deferred = STILL OWED: your terminal answer reads degraded/best_effort until you re-disposition this exact child_result_sha256. Integrated/irrelevant also let the host release the child's disposable scratch; until then it waits for your end, Continues included: while a step or sibling reads it by a path you passed (the host cannot see such paths), stay deferred or save what must outlive it.",
          "enum": [
            "deferred",
            "integrated",
            "irrelevant"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        "evidence_ref": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "evidence_sha256": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "rationale": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "scope": {},
        "type": {
          "enum": [
            "child_result_disposition"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "text": {
      "description": "Short coordination text (<=4000 chars).",
      "maxLength": 4000,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "kind",
    "text"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## update_identity

Revise my identity manifest, who I am and who I want to become, after substantive reflection: one file in every room; never write memory/identity.md through file tools. Change parts with mode='edit': edits=[{old_str, new_str}, ...] (or one old_str with content), each old_str exact text found once in the revision I read, all applied or none, an empty new_str deleting; mode='overwrite' (default) replaces the whole text with content; mode='revert' puts back version=<revision> exactly. expected_revision (the revision under my resident identity) is required; a stale one writes nothing and returns what changed since. The result is never empty; reason is kept in history, not in the text. The receipt names the version replaced, who wrote it and what left, with the calls that read it (memory_read(source='identity', version=...)) and put it back.

        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "new_str": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "old_str": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "old_str",
          "new_str"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "expected_revision": {
      "description": "The current revision (under the resident identity, or a receipt's or refusal's).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "mode": {
      "enum": [
        "overwrite",
        "edit",
        "revert"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "new_str": {
      "description": "old_str's replacement, as content (empty deletes).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "old_str": {
      "description": "mode=edit, one pair: exact text found once.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reason": {
      "description": "Why: kept in history, never in the text.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "version": {

    }

}

## update_scratchpad

## vcs_read

Read local Git status, diff, history, files, blame, refs, ancestry, or repository identity. root/repository selects a worktree; path filters within it. No fetch. Diff uses configured filters: base compares to worktree (or index with staged); base+head compares two trees. Identity is sequential observations, not proof of an exact staged subject. History output has a physical capture bound; narrow with max_count, ref, or path.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "blame",
        "diff",
        "file",
        "identity",
        "log",
        "merge_base",
        "refs",
        "rev_parse",
        "show",
        "status"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "base": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "First revision for merge_base, or diff base resolved once to a tree.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "head": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "Second revision for merge_base or diff; diff requires base and staged=false.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "max_chars": {
      "default": 0,
      "description": "Rendered character limit; zero adds no limit beyond the history capture bound.",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "max_count": {
      "default": 20,
      "description": "Maximum commits returned by log.",
      "maximum": 200,
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "name_only": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Changed file names only, for diff or show; takes precedence over stat.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "path": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "Repository-relative path filter (a pathspec for status/diff, literal for history); required for file and blame.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ref": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "Local revision (default HEAD), or a literal refs/ prefix for refs.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "repository": {
      "default": "",

## vcs_revert

Undo one commit by creating a revert commit. confirm=false previews; true requires a clean worktree. Refuses merge commits. In Ouroboros's own repository, protected-path reverts follow the caller's effective runtime mode (task limits included) or existing managed-update authority. Mechanical revert requires no new review.

## vcs_rollback

Roll Ouroboros's own running checkout (its current branch) back to a tag or commit SHA through the supervisor's Rollback procedure (the UI Restore button): every running task is interrupted, a rescue snapshot of uncommitted changes is created, the server restarts. Review-exempt mechanical recovery; the target's review status and compatibility are not guaranteed.

}
```

## verify_and_record

Verify BEFORE claiming completion; the host runs your check and records a durable attested receipt, replacing a separate verification run. contract_kind: visible_verifier/explicit_command run check and pass on exit 0 plus any expected substring; explicit_metric runs check and requires the expected metric string; artifact_observation confirms artifact_paths exist; no_visible_machine_contract records your best proxy and risk for review when no machine check exists; delegation_zero_run records an incomplete/unknown decision for configured session actors whose physical leaf never started (zero_run_decision + zero_run_basis). Verify against the task's own statement and materials, your human's words, installed oracles and your independent checks.

Run kinds (visible_verifier/explicit_command/explicit_metric) also check after execution that paths RELATIVE to cwd still exist; advisory artifact_lifecycle flags expose checks that delete their deliverables.",

      },

        "array",
        "string"
      ]
    },
    "contract_kind": {

      "enum": [
        "visible_verifier",

    "cwd": {

      "description": "Match expected as substring (default), exact (whole stripped output), exact_line (one stripped output line), or json_equals (parsed JSON equality, ignoring key order). bytes_equal compares artifact_paths=[a, b] byte-for-byte after check, recording a bounded hexdump of the first divergence (golden files/migration parity). Prefer stricter matching for worked examples/exact output.",
      "enum": [

## view_image

Bring a LOCAL image file natively into your own context so you can SEE and reason about it directly (vision-capable models). Resource class: local_file_to_model — it reads a local file and attaches it into your context; it is NOT a web tool and works even when web/network access is disabled. LOCAL PATHS ONLY (inside the task workspace, uploads dir, or the task's artifact_store/task_drive — e.g. frames from extract_video_frames under artifact_store/video_frames, or staged attachments under artifact_store/attachments); no URLs. Typical flow: after list_files reveals an image file (.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp) — including one you rendered yourself, e.g. a chart or a rendered toolpath — call view_image(path) and then analyze it inline. Prefer this over vlm_query when you need to reason about the image yourself rather than ask a separate model.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "Local image path: relative to the active workspace (list_files' default root), or absolute inside the workspace, uploads dir, the skill-state tree (data/state/skills) or the task's artifact_store/task_drive (e.g. a frame path extract_video_frames returned).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## vlm_query

Ask a vision model, in a separate call, to analyze one image (not your own native view; see view_image). Provide one of: file_path (local file, preferred — avoids large base64 in arguments), image_url (public URL), or image_base64 (base64-encoded PNG/JPEG). Use file_path for files already on disk (e.g. data/uploads/ attachments). Use for: analyzing charts, reading diagrams, understanding screenshots, checking UI. NOTE: this DELEGATES to a separate vision model — when you are vision-capable yourself, prefer view_image (native inline vision, no second-model handoff) for anything you need to REASON about rather than merely describe.

## wait_task

Wait for ONE subtask to reach a terminal status and return its effective result: the full single-child handoff once it settled (or when your known_result_sha256 no longer matches); a return BEFORE it settled carries the compact wait_tasks projection plus delegated_runs (its open delegated runs: the observation the host records when a run's state or the engine's answer changes, dated by when that began, never per read, so no date proves a recent read; no liveness verdict). May return EARLY (before terminal) if the child raises a tree_note blocker/question/interface_contract/review_requested/delegation_constraint beacon — the result then carries a [CHILD_BEACONS] block so you can steer, review, or override it. Unread mailbox messages return early for the ordinary loop to deliver and acknowledge; host-marked context-only place arrivals stay unread until a genuine wake. The child keeps running. A child held by a current stop you have not yet been shown returns once with [HELD_DEPENDENCY] (its current_stop: cause, who releases it, the request door if yours); waiting again keeps waiting. Omitting sleep_mode sleeps even with timeout_sec (the wake time); saved state/obligations release your process unless live custody keeps it warm, named in the receipt. The result reaches your first request after wake. Explicit in_slot keeps the process and same-call result while yielding acting capacity; warm/cold choose the sleep mode. With SEVERAL children in flight, prefer wait_tasks(any_terminal) to absorb whichever finishes first rather than blocking serially on one id at a time.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "known_result_sha256": {
      "description": "Prior child_result_sha256 in every view; current facts still refresh. This does not change when the wait ends.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "sleep_mode": {
      "description": "Omitted: you sleep; your process is released once nothing live keeps it (what does is named and the process stays) and timeout_sec is the wake time. in_slot keeps the process/call, yielding acting capacity. warm keeps your process; cold saves your continuation and releases it (non-transferable work refuses it). A sleep wakes when this wait is satisfied, a waited child raises an attention beacon, addressed mail or owner input arrives or an executor of yours asks a question, and the wait's result then reaches your next request. A selected task whose record is lost wakes it as unknown, never success.",
      "enum": [
        "in_slot",
        "warm",
        "cold"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_id": {
      "description": "Task ID to check",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "timeout_sec": {
      "description": "With no sleep_mode: the sleep's wake time, in seconds. With sleep_mode=in_slot: maximum seconds to wait (default 180); a larger value is clamped to 3600, and a deadline narrows it (named in the result). Size the window to the child's expected life.",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "view": {
      "description": "Settled result view; omitted/full preserves the existing handoff. Early returns remain compact wait observations, not a result or full read.",
      "enum": [
        "answer",
        "summary",
        "evidence",
        "full"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "wake_after_sec": {
      "description": "A sleep only (not in_slot): also wake to inspect after this many seconds (not with wake_at). Omit to wake on events.",
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "wake_at": {
      "description": "A sleep only (not in_slot): an absolute ISO-8601 inspection time with timezone.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "task_id"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## wait_tasks

Wait for MULTIPLE subtasks at once: the right tool to ABSORB a batch of independent children you scheduled in one burst. With mode=any_terminal it returns as soon as the FIRST child finishes (handle it, then call again for the rest) instead of blocking serially. Each child gets a compact structural projection, its cost as accounted_upper_bound_usd with cost_final; the full per-child envelope stays in the task store (child_result_sha256 pins the exact result you saw; get_task_result returns the full result text plus trace/outcome summaries). The wait may early_return (before all terminal) on a child tree_note blocker/question/interface_contract/review_requested/delegation_constraint beacon so you can steer, review, or override mid-flight, or on unread mailbox messages (reason=owner_mailbox_pending); host-marked context-only place arrivals stay unread until a genuine wake. The ordinary loop handles delivery and acknowledgement. A child held by a current stop you have not yet been shown returns once (reason=dependency_held); waiting again keeps waiting. An id no surface of this tree ever minted (no task result, queue row or tree-ledger row) is flagged unknown_task_id ('not yet registered or never scheduled'), with unknown_task_ids and a compact children_roster of your ACTUAL direct children so you can repair the wait set instead of re-polling phantoms. Omitting sleep_mode sleeps even with timeout_sec (the wake time); unminted ids are then refused. Saved state/obligations release your process unless named live custody keeps it warm; the result reaches your first request after wake. Explicit in_slot keeps the process and same-call result while yielding acting capacity; warm/cold choose the sleep mode.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "known_result_sha256_by_task": {
      "additionalProperties": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "description": "Optional task_id to previously obtained child_result_sha256 map. Matching children omit only result/trace and return result_unchanged plus a full-read reference. Missing or different hashes return the usual complete body/trace. Current status/cost/outcome/capability facts remain; wait timing is unchanged.",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "mode": {
      "default": "all_terminal",
      "enum": [
        "all_terminal",
        "any_terminal"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "sleep_mode": {
      "description": "Omitted: you sleep; your process is released once nothing live keeps it (what does is named and the process stays) and timeout_sec is the wake time. in_slot keeps the process/call, yielding acting capacity. warm keeps your process; cold saves your continuation and releases it (non-transferable work refuses it). A sleep wakes when this wait is satisfied, a waited child raises an attention beacon, addressed mail or owner input arrives or an executor of yours asks a question, and the wait's result then reaches your next request. A selected task whose record is lost wakes it as unknown, never success.",
      "enum": [
        "in_slot",
        "warm",
        "cold"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "task_ids": {
      "description": "Task IDs returned by schedule_subagent.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "timeout_sec": {
      "description": "With no sleep_mode: the sleep's wake time, in seconds. With sleep_mode=in_slot: maximum seconds to wait (default 600); a larger value is clamped to 7200. Size the window to the children's expected life; an expired wait returns the still-live ids and this ceiling; a deadline narrows it (window_bound).",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "view": {
      "description": "Optional: each settled child in this get_task_result view instead of the compact projection; unsettled children stay compact. Omitted keeps the compact batch.",
      "enum": [
        "answer",
        "summary",
        "evidence",
        "full"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "wake_after_sec": {
      "description": "A sleep only (not in_slot): also wake to inspect after this many seconds (not with wake_at). Omit to wake on events.",
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "wake_at": {
      "description": "A sleep only (not in_slot): an absolute ISO-8601 inspection time with timezone.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "task_ids"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

## workpad_write

Write the current project's workpad, a working page for plans, links and state (durable facts belong in knowledge_write, history in journal_write). Change parts with mode='edit': edits=[{old_str, new_str}, ...] (or one old_str with content), each old_str exact text found once in the revision I read, all or none; mode='overwrite' (default) replaces the whole page with content; mode='revert' puts back version=<revision>. expected_revision (shown under the resident page and by workpad_read) is required for edit and revert; an overwrite without it still lands, and replacing a version this task did not write answers with a warning. A stale revision writes nothing and returns what changed since. reason is kept in the page's history. The receipt states the page's size (it enters every request of its project whole), what it replaced and the calls that read it (memory_read(source='workpad:<project id>', version=...)) and put it back.

```json
{
  "properties": {
    "content": {
      "description": "overwrite: the whole new page; edit with old_str: its replacement.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "edits": {
      "description": "mode=edit: exact {old_str, new_str} items, all or none.",
      "items": {
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "new_str": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "old_str": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "old_str",
          "new_str"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "minItems": 1,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "expected_revision": {
      "description": "The current revision (under the resident page, workpad_read's, a receipt's or refusal's); empty creates a missing page only.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "mode": {
      "enum": [
        "overwrite",
        "edit",
        "revert"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "new_str": {
      "description": "old_str's replacement, as content (empty deletes).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "old_str": {
      "description": "mode=edit, one pair: exact text found once.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "project_id": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "Explicit project id (defaults to the current task's project scope).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reason": {
      "description": "Why: kept in history, never in the text.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "version": {
      "description": "mode=revert: the revision to put back.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [],
  "type": "object"
}
```
